The Adjustable Chain Gearshift functions similarly to Encased Chain Drive, but can change the speed of the output when powered with redstone.

Adjustable Chain Gearshift

Usage[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Usage of the Adjustable Chain Gearshift 		 	 
To control the speed of an encased chain, the Adjustable Chain Gearshift must be placed in line with Encased Chain Drives with sides touching. 
To increase the speed of an encased chain, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift must be connected to the source of rotational power by its axis and it must be powered by a redstone signal. A full strength redstone signal will double the speed of the chain.  A partial strength signal, such as given by an analog lever, will give a proportional increase in speed between 1x and 2x.
If a redstone-powered Adjustable Chain Gearshift receives its rotational power from an encased chain, then it will reduce the rotation speed of its axis by up to half, again depending on the strength of the redstone signal.

Examples[]
Other means to apply RPM ratios only make it possible to double or halve the speed (using cogwheels, Sequenced Gearshifts...). Using combinations of the speed ratios above, it is theoretically possible to approach any RPM ratio, and therefore any RPM.
For example, when trying to build a real time clock, Clockwork Bearings can't be used (they display in-game time instead). A Mechanical Bearing spinning at 1 RPM works for the second hand, because it has to perform 1 full cycle of the clock per minute. However, the minute hand should be 60 times slower, running at 1/60 RPM, and the hour hand 12 times slower than the minute hand. To reach ratios of 60:1 and 12:1, which are not powers of 2, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift is required. A working combination in that case is:

Decrease speed at a ratio of 15:8 with power 13, and halve the speed 5 times (32:1). The result is a ratio of 480:8 = 60:1.
Decrease speed at a ratio of 3:2 with power 7, and halve the speed 3 times (8:1). The result is a ratio of 24:2 = 12:1.
In a niche use case, you need to perform a rotation of 1 radian. To get an accurate angle, a Valve Handle can be used, but they only work in degrees. There are exactly π radians in 180 degrees, so applying a ratio of approximately π:1 to a Valve Handle set to 180 degrees would work. This process can get quite tedious, especially for situations like this with no obvious solution, that require chained Adjustable Chain Gearshifts. In that case, the RPM Ratio Finder is an online tool that can help find a working combination. Below is an example for a π:1 ratio.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			A valid combination approaching a π:1 ratio, provided by the RPM Ratio Finder. The numbers are the redstone power to feed the Adjustable Chain Gearshifts.

The Adjustable Crate is a block that stores Items.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Crafting


2 Usage

2.1 Container


3 History



Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Adjustable Crate

Brass Casing

4



Usage[]
Much like a Chest, an Adjustable Crate placed next to another crate will form a larger crate equivalent in storage to two individual crates.

Container[]
An adjustable crate has 16 slots of inventory space, and two combined crates have 32 slots of inventory space.
Crates open when used and, unlike chests, can be opened when there is an opaque block above them.
The storage space of a crate can be adjusted by scrolling with the cursor over the second number of the crate's GUI. Holding shift while scrolling will adjust by one slot (64 items) at a time.
When an adjustable crate is filled with items that do not stack to 64, the number of items in the crate can show as being less than the maximum, while still not allowing more items to be placed inside.

History[]
0.4: Removed.
0.2: Renamed to Adjustable Crates.
0.1: Introduced as FlexCrates.

Perfectly Stressed

Get a 100% readout from a Stressometer

Mixing it up

Look at a Stressometer reading exactly 100% stress while wearing Engineer's Goggles.

 The Parrots and the Flaps

Make two belt mounted funnels kiss.

Mixing it up

Place two Funnels adjacent and facing each other on belts, then right-click both with a Wrench so they touch.

create:belt_funnel_kiss



	
		
		

	


 Magma Wheel

This shouldn't have worked.

Mixing it up

Make a waterwheel spin using Lava.

create:lava_wheel



	
		
		

	


Workout Session

Use a Hand Crank until fully exhausted

Mixing it up

Run out of Hunger while turning a Hand Crank.

create:hand_crank_000



	
		
		

	


Swimming with the Striders

Attempt to take a dive in lava with your Netherite Diving Gear

Pressure to Go

Completely submerge in Lava while wearing a Netherite Diving Helmet, Netherite Diving Boots and Netherite Backtank.

create:diving_suit_lava



	
		
		

	


The Pipe Organ

Attach 12 uniquely pitched Steam Whistles to a single fluid tank

Pressure to Go

Place a Fluid Tank and attach 12 uniquely pitched Steam Whistles.

create:pipe_organ



	
		
		

	


 On a Roll

Watch an item roll across several chained item drains.

Pressure to Go

Watch an item roll across at least two Item Drains in a row.

 Don't cross the streams!

Watch two fluids meet in your pipe network

Place a Fluid Pipe and try to channel 2 different fluids through it at once.

Trivia[]
The Chute’s “Tumbling Down” advancement is possibly a reference to the song used in the popular Japanese movie The End of Evangelion
The Chocolate Bucket's "A world of Imagination" advancement is possibly a reference to the song Pure Imagination from the movie Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory , as one of the song's lyrics is "In a world of pure imagination"
The Rotation Speed Controller's "Engineers hate him!" achievement is possibly a reference to the phrase "Doctors hate him", which is often used in pop-up ads.
The Polished Rose Quartz' "Pink Diamonds" achievement is possibly a reference to Steven Universe, as Rose Quartz and Pink Diamond are revealed to be the same character in season 5

Usage[]
The lever emits a redstone signal with an adjustable strength. Right click to make it higher, shift right click to make it lower. The current signal strength can be viewed by looking at the lever while wearing Engineer's Goggles. Different pitched clicks can be heard when lowering or heightening the strength; similar to a Note Block.

Andesite Alloy is a material used in Andesite Casing and simple kinetic blocks, which serves as an entry-point to the mechanical components of Create.  Among its many functions, it is an essential ingredient for crafting Shafts and both regular and large Cogwheels. Andesite Alloy is the most basic component construction material in Create.

The Andesite Funnel is used to extract or insert materials into inventories, similar in nature to the Brass Funnel.


Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Crafting


2 Usage

2.1 Placement
2.2 Input/Output


3 Data values

3.1 ID


4 History



Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Andesite Funnel

Andesite Alloy +Dried Kelp

2



Usage[]
While held, funnels prevent the player from accessing inventories, instead placing them.

Placement[]
Sneak right clicking with a Funnel places it in input mode.
Right-clicking a funnel on a Mechanical Belt causes it to extend one block forward.
When attached to a Contraption, Andesite Funnels can drop items from the contraption's inventory or pick up items that collide with it.

Input/Output[]
When outputting to dropped items, the Funnel waits until the previous dropped item is removed before dropping another stack.
The Andesite Funnel outputs only one item at a time, but can input entire stacks.
When not on a Mechanical Belt, a Wrench can be used to set it to extract or insert. Otherwise, the direction of the belt determines whether the Funnel extracts or inserts.
Redstone can be applied to stop the funnel from inputting or outputting.

Some items can't be crafted normally in a mechanical crafter or a crafting table, and sometimes they need to be pressed or washed. Automation of items is a basic in game concept that needs to be mastered to move on. In create some items needs to be assembled on an Assembly Line. Lets say you want to make a Precision Mechanism. First you have to use a deployer to apply a cog on a gold sheet then apply a large cog then an iron nugget. Repeat 5 times and you will make the item.

disclaimer there is only a 80% chance of a  Precision Mechanism being made when you complete the process the other 20% is the  Precision Mechanism breaks .  Precision Mechanism are also the easiest item to automate other then iron

The Basin is a block that holds items and fluids used in Packing, Compacting, and Mixing recipes. A Basin can also function as an interaction point in fluid systems as fluids can be placed in or removed from a Basin directly by a player. In a survival game, a Basin's most significant function is creating Brass, which is essential for the creation of most advanced components.

Contents

1 Crafting
2 Usage

2.1 Packing, Compacting, and Mixing
2.2 Inventory
2.3 Fluid Logistics


3 Data values

3.1 ID


4 History



Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Basin

Andesite Alloy





Usage[]
Packing, Compacting, and Mixing[]
Basins can be used in conjunction with a Mechanical Mixer to apply Mixing recipes and with a Mechanical Press to apply Packing and Compacting recipes. If a Basin is placed two blocks below a powered Mechanical Mixer or Mechanical Press, the mixer or press will activate as soon as the basin contains all the ingredients for a valid recipe. 
A Basin's filter slot can be used to restrict which recipes will be performed. Right-click the filter slot with the desired item to set the filter. 

Inventory[]
A Basin can contain both items and fluids. A Basin can contain up to 16 of each item and up to 1000 mB of each fluid. Items can be added by hoppers, funnels, and Chutes, and fluids can be added by Fluid Pipes and by Deployers holding buckets and bottles. Basins can also take in items floating in the world in and directly above their block space. Players can interact with a basin's fluid inventory in a similar manner to vanilla cauldrons.
Some mixing recipes (including that of Brass) require a heated or super-heated Blaze Burner to be directly underneath the basin.
A Basin can output its item products to another Basin, a Mechanical Belt, a Depot, a Chute, a pair of Crushing Wheels, or an Item Drain. A Basin can output fluid products to another Basin or an Item Drain. Additionally, Basin will drop all of its items when flipped upside down in a contraption. 

The destination of the output must be in the block directly below an air block directly next to the basin.
If a Basin has a valid output destination, a spout will appear on the side of the Basin, "pouring" the items out of the Basin and to the destination. If multiple output destinations are possible, right-clicking the Basin with a Wrench will change the location of the spout.
Fluid Logistics[]
Since fluids in Basins can be added and removed directly by players, Basins provide a valuable interaction point with fluid logistics systems. For instance, it can allow players to manually fill or empty a Fluid Tank connected to a basin by a Mechanical Pump.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Outputting a potion of weakness from a mixer-basin 		 	 
To extract a fluid from a pipe, such as a potion, without also extracting the inputted water use a smart fluid pipe. Create and apply a filter set to blacklist water (using a water bucket). Then use a mechanical pump to draw the fluid along into a second basin. From there you can send it to a spout if desired.

Usage[]
In-Game Tooltip[]
Detects items and entities passing by on a Mechanical Belt in front of it. Use a Wrench to cycle its behaviour. Non-items will always be handled in detect mode regardless of the setting. 
Detect Mode 
Provides redstone while a matching item is in the observed belt segment. 
Pulse Mode 
Emits a pulse when a matching item passes the center of the observed belt segment. 
Eject Mode 
Ejects matching items off the side. If the target belt or space is occupied, the item will be held in place. 
Split Mode 
Splits a matching item stack and ejects half of it off the side.

A Blaze Burner is a heating component that is required for certain Mixing recipes. It can be used for heating Steam Engines, Bulk Smoking, Bulk Smelting, and as a decorative light source.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Crafting an Empty Blaze Burner
1.2 Filling an Empty Blaze Burner


2 Usage

2.1 Heating
2.2 Train Controlling


3 Decoration
4 Data values

4.1 ID


5 Gallery
6 History



Obtaining[]
Crafting an Empty Blaze Burner[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Empty Blaze Burner

Iron Sheet +Netherrack





Filling an Empty Blaze Burner[]
Blaze Burners must have Blazes in them to function. To put a Blaze in an Empty Blaze Burner, right-click on a Blaze while holding an Empty Blaze Burner. Alternatively, an Empty Blaze Burner can be filled by right-clicking on a Blaze Spawner. This method can be repeated without risk of destroying the Blaze Spawner.

Usage[]
Heating[]
Blaze Burners are used for Heating and Super-Heating Basins when doing Mixing recipes. In particular, they are required to make Brass. They can also be used as a heat source for boilers used to power Steam Engines. When a heat-able block is placed above a fueled Blaze Burner, the Burner will appear to channel heat into the block.
Right-clicking a Blaze Burner with any item that can be used as Furnace fuel will temporarily put it in a Heated state. Right-clicking a Blaze Burner with a Blaze Cake will temporarily put it in a Super-Heated state.
Fuel burn time is the same as a vanilla Furnace. The Blaze inside changes its size and texture depending on the amount of fuel provided, following the phases:

Phase 1 — Smouldering — Does not provide any heat for mixing, but provides the "passive" heat level for boilers (for more details see Heat sources). This is the default state when placing the Burner or when the fuel runs out.
Phase 2 — Heated/Kindled — Enables recipes that require heating. Lasts for the fuel's burn time and provides 1 heating level to Steam Engines per Blaze Burner
Phase 3 — Super-Heated/Seething — Enables every Mixing recipe and provides 2 heating levels to Steam Engines per Blaze Burner. Only achievable using the Blaze Cake. Always lasts for 160 seconds. The Blaze Burner cannot be re-fed during this phase.
Throwing an Egg at it will also generate heat. This is a reference to Howl's Moving Castle, as the Blaze Burners look similar to Calcifer.
A Deployer or Mechanical Arm can be used to automatically fuel the blaze burner by giving it a burnable item as input. If lava is used, the bucket will not be consumed. They will stop adding fuel if the Blaze Burner's remaining burn time is over 500 seconds, so no fuel is wasted. The exception to this is lava, which will be refueled at (and waste) 20 seconds, since lava completely fills the burner's maximum capacity of 1000 seconds.

Train Controlling[]
When assembled with a Train and given a Train Schedule, it will drive the Train to the Train Stations the schedule specifies.

Decoration[]
Blaze Burners can be given a set of Engineer's Goggles by right-clicking them with goggles in hand. This does not consume the goggles, and is purely cosmetic.
Empty Blaze Burners can be lit on fire with a Flint and Steel as a decorative block. While lit, they can be given Soul Sand or Soul Soil to turn the fire into Soul Fire. These do not serve as heat for mixer recipes. However, they can be used as a passive heat source for Steam Engine boilers and for Bulk Smoking and Bulk Haunting using the lit and soul fire versions respectively.

The Block of Copper is a decorative storage block equivalent to nine Copper Ingots.

Cut Copper, Copper Shingles, and Copper Tiles are purely decorative variants of the copper block and cannot be converted back into ingot form.

Contents

2.3.2 Adjustable Chain Gearshift


2.4 Rotation Speed Controller

3 Contraption Controllers

3.1 Mechanical Piston

3.5.1 Minecart Contraptions
3.5.2 Carriage Contraptions







Mod spotlights[]
Mod spotlight by direwolf20 are YouTube videos introducing Create concepts and features. Note that the videos describe an earlier version of Create and many features have been updated: Part 1, Part 2, Part 3. Part 4

The Basics of Rotation[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			A Rotating Encased belt block 		 	 
Many machines and components in Create require Rotational Force to operate. Rotational force is generated by several Kinetic Sources such as the  Hand Crank and the  Water Wheel. Rotation can then be transmitted to Kinetic Appliances which perform a variety of actions with items such as a  Crushing Wheel or a  Mechanical Saw.
Rotational force has three characteristics: direction (clockwise, counter clockwise), speed in revolutions per minute (rpm), and Kinetic Stress (or power) measured in Stress Units (SU). Kinetic sources provide a specific number of stress units depending on the configuration of the source. Each kinetic appliance uses a certain number of stress units depending on the type of appliance and rotational speed. When the total number of stress units required by the attached appliances exceeds the number of stress units provided by the kinetic source, the kinetic source stops completely until the required stress units are reduced.

Generating Rotational Force[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Simple Windmill 		 	 Main Article: Generators
Transmitting Rotational Force[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Transmitting power with shafts, belts, cogs and gearboxes. 		 	 
Rotation can be transmitted in a straight line using a  Shaft,  Mechanical Belt, or  Encased Chain Drive. The direction can be turned 90 degrees using a   Gearbox or  Large Cogwheel. The rotation can be temporarily stopped using a   Clutch and can be reversed with a   Gearshift
The image to the right illustrates rotational power coming in from the top left via a length of connected shafts. The direction is turned 90 degrees downward using two large cogwheels. The vertical shaft then powers a gearbox that turns the direction of rotation to the right where a series of cogwheels, mechanical belts and gearboxes power a  Deployer, a  Mechanical Press, and a  Mechanical Mixer.
These transmission components only transfer, stop, or convert rotational power. They do not consume any power [Unless changed in the Config] or change the speed of rotation.

Changing Speed[]
Just having components rotate is not always enough. Sometimes it is necessary to control the speed of rotation. This is especially important for machines that require a minimum level of speed to operate (e.g. the Mechanical Mixer). To make this possible, some kinetic blocks have the ability to speed up or slow down connected components:

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Changing Speed with Cogwheels 		 	 
Cogwheels[]
Cogwheels are not only useful for relaying rotation, but also serve as a simple way to control the speed. By attaching a large cogwheel diagonally to a regular sized one, one can double/half the speed of the other.
Powering the large cogwheel results in the smaller one turning at double the speed.
Powering the small cogwheel results in the larger one turning at half the speed.


Adjustable Chain Gearshift[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Adjustable chain gearshift doubling the speed of an encased chain. 		 	 
The  Adjustable Chain Gearshift when used in combination with  Encased Chain Drives, gives finer control over speed than cogwheels. It can increase input speed for attached chain drives, or decrease output speed of shafts connected to chain drives.
While acting as an input, the adjustable chain gearshift will increase the speed of attached encased chain drives based on the analog redstone signal it receives. A full power redstone signal of 15 will double the speed of the chain drives while values below 15 will increase the speed proportionally between 1x and 2x. While acting as an output, it will reduce the speed of the chain drive in a similar manner. With no redstone signal, the speed will remain unchanged.

Rotation Speed Controller[]
While having a more expensive recipe, the  Rotation Speed Controller also has the finest control over speed change. When a large cogwheel is attached to the controllers top, the large cogwheel, or shaft [depending on which one is powered] will spin at the configured speed in the Values Settings Screen. 

Stress Units[]
Most kinetic appliances will consume SU (Stress Units).    

These blocks include:
Mechanical Piston (sticky and non-sticky)
Mechanical Press
Millstone
Crushing Wheels
Mechanical Mixers
Mechanical Saw
Deployer
Mechanical Drill
Mechanical Crafter
Rope Pulley
Clockwork Bearing
Mechanical Bearing
Encased Fan
Cuckoo Clock
Materials[]
Create adds many crafting ingredients for use throughout the mod. While some of them have few uses within Create itself at the moment, they are still handy connection points for pack-makers.    

Andesite Alloy, used for Andesite Casing and all the low-tier kinetic components.
Brass, used in Brass Casing and more advanced kinetic blocks. Entry-point to the logistical components.
Copper, generates in the world around surface level. Used for Copper Casing and fluid handling components, and used with Zinc to make Brass.
Zinc, generates in the world. Used with Copper to make Brass.
Other Materials[]
Cinder Flour, made from crushing Netherrack. Non renewable without 3rd party addons.
Polished Rose Quartz, made from using Sand Paper on craft-able Rose Quartz. Used in the crafting of Electron Tubes and mixing of Chromatic Compound.
Powdered Obsidian, made from crushing Obsidian. Used in several filling recipes and in the compacting of Blaze Cake Bases.
Moving Contraptions[]
Create allows you to move and animate block structures of any shape or form. This feature is extremely powerful as it proves useful in the field of automation, transportation and aesthetics.
In order to get the most out of this mechanic, it is helpful to know about the components and interactions involved in creating such structures.    

Contraption Controllers
Contraption Assembly and Chassis Blocks
Portable Storage
Portable Actors
Contraption Controllers[]
Depending on the use case, different controllers can be used for mounting your structure. Some push, some pull, some rotate and some do it all at once.
These blocks have specific spaces where the anchor of the structure needs to be, and some can be configured to react differently to being stopped.
Mechanical Piston[]
Mechanical Pistons are kinetically powered counterparts to Minecraft's Pistons. As such, they can push super glued blocks in front of them, and if sticky, pull them back.
However, Create's pistons do not work on their own. They require Piston Extension Poles added at the back, in order to be able to extend. When given Rotational Force, the piston will extend exactly as far as poles have been added to the back, rather than just 1 block space.

Rope Pulley[]
The Rope Pulley moves attached blocks and structures vertically. Use Linear Chassis, Radial Chassis or Super Glue to move more than a single block. 
When powered by kinetics, it will start to move the attached structure. Speed and direction correlate to the incoming Rotation Speed.

Mechanical Bearing[]
The Mechanical Bearing is used for rotating larger structures with rotational force.
When Powered by kinetics, starts rotating the attached blocks.
Use Chassis or Super Glue to move more than a single block. Blocks that attach to other blocks, such as levers, torches, Gantry Shafts or Mechanical Saws will become part of the structure automatically.
Other attached Mechanical Bearings, if facing along the same axis as the original, will keep their alignment as the original rotates: See the GIFs for a visual example.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Clockwork Bearing[]
The Clockwork Bearing is an advanced version of the Mechanical Bearing for rotating up to two clock hands according to the current in-game time.
When powered by kinetics, starts rotating the attached structure towards the current hour. If an independent second structure exists in front of the first one, it will serve as the minute hand.

Cart Assembler[]
When placed on a Rail, the Cart Assembler can assemble and disassemble moving structures onto passing minecarts. Similarly to rotating structures, having a Mechanical Bearing in the structure will cause the attached part to keep the same alignment as the cart moves.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	  
Minecart Contraptions[]
Single Cart contraptions as well as Carriage contraptions can carry items, liquids, or mobs, provided they have the correct storage blocks. They can also use Contrapion Actors such as the Mechanical Saw, Drill, Harvester, Plough or the Portable Storage Interface to interact with the world.

Carriage Contraptions[]
Carriage Contraptions are about the same, except their movement is smoother and thus it is easier to walk or ride on them without falling off. See Trains for further detail.

The Brass Funnel  is a block that can extract or insert items into inventories, much like the Andesite Funnel.

Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Brass Funnel

Brass Ingot +Electron Tube +Dried Kelp

2



Usage[]
Placement[]
 	https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Funnel_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scenes for the Funnel. 		 	 
Funnels can be placed on inventories without the need to sneak, being placed in output mode by default. Sneaking while placing will place the funnel in input mode.
Funnels placed on a Mechanical Belt input or output depending on the belt's direction. A Wrench can be used to extend the funnel forwards.
When attached to a Contraption, Brass Funnels can drop items from the contraption's inventory or pick up items that collide with it. The filter is respected.

Filtering[]
Like other Brass machines, the Brass Funnel can be set to Filter items. It can also be set to output or input either "exactly" or "up to" a set amount of items via its Value Settings Screen.

Input/Output[]
When outputting to dropped items, the Funnel waits until the previous dropped item is removed before dropping another stack.
When not on a Mechanical Belt, a Wrench can be used to set it to extract or insert. Otherwise, the direction of the belt determines whether the Funnel extracts or inserts.
It can be turned off with Redstone.

A Brass Tunnel is a machine that can only be placed on Mechanical Belts. It can be decorative or it can be used to split, sort, or combine streams of items fed by belts.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Crafting


2 Usage

2.1 Value Settings
2.2 Splitting Item Streams to Multiple Destinations
2.3 Item Sorting
2.4 Combining Multiple Item Streams


3 Data values

3.1 ID


4 History



Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Brass Tunnel

Electron Tube +Brass Ingot +Dried Kelp

2



Usage[]
Brass Tunnels may be used on mechanical belts for four functions: 1) purely decorative, 2) splitting streams of items to multiple destinations, 3) sorting streams of items, and 4) combining multiple streams of items. Each tunnel can have an input or output portal on each of its four sides in a variety of combinations. The status of being an input or output depends purely on the direction of the belt touching a given side. A tunnel must straddle a belt, thus forcing at least one input and one output on opposite sides. The other two sides may have belts abutting the tunnel forming either input or output portals.
Tunnels which are placed immediately next to each other are automatically treated as a group, in most cases collecting from all inputs and distributing to all outputs. The way that items are distributed is controlled by the tunnels' value setting. Item stacks from different inputs will not be combined prior to distributing.

Value Settings[]
The Value Settings Screen can be accessed from the top of a tunnel. It is only viewable if the tunnel has more than two portals or is connected to other tunnels. All tunnels connected as a group will have the same value setting.



Setting

Split Stack?

Pause when blocked?

Function


Split

Yes

No

Each item stack will be split evenly between available outputs.


Forced Split

Yes

Yes

Each item stack will be split evenly. All output is paused when any output is blocked.


Round Robin

No

No

Keeps input stacks together and routes each successive stack to the next available output in turn. Successive outputs progress clockwise.


Forced Round Robin

No

Yes

Keeps input stacks together. Alternates among the available outputs pausing at any blocked output until it is cleared.


Prefer Nearest

No

No

Chooses the output nearest to the input for as long as it is available. If there are multiple inputs, each input is routed separately to its nearest output. If a tunnel receiving an input has multiple outputs then the output on the right side is considered nearest, followed by the output on the left and finally the output across from the input.


Randomize

No

No

Output is randomized.


Synchronize Inputs

No

No

Takes inputs simultaneously from all available input ports. If any of the ports do not have an item ready to be taken, all inputs will pause. Each tunnel routes its input separately to its nearest output.

Splitting Item Streams to Multiple Destinations[]
The Split, Forced Split, Round Robin, Forced Round Robin, and Randomize modes can be used to split one or more item input streams into multiple output streams. For example, a stream of logs may be split with half going to the fuel chamber of a furnace and half going to the smelting chamber. The Forced Split mode causes the output streams to have a nearly equal number of items while the Forced Round Robin causes the output streams to have nearly equal numbers of stacks. The Split and Round Robin will also keep the items or stacks evenly distributed as long as none of the outputs become obstructed. If that happens, the output will continue at the unobstructed ports. If single items rather than stacks enter a tunnel, the Split and Forced Split will default to Round Robin and Forced Round Robin behavior.

Item Sorting[]
Brass Tunnels can be Filtered to only allow certain items to pass. By placing different filters on the outputs of individual tunnels in a group, the cumulative input can be sorted. All items matching a filter will only pass through an output with that matching filter. They will not pass through an unfiltered output. Unfiltered outputs will pass all items that do not have a matching filter. If a particular filter is set on multiple tunnel outputs, then the distribution of the applicable items among the matching outputs will follow the value setting mode. Each group of outputs with common filters will apply the value setting mode independently.
Each individual tunnel within a group has its own space to hold an input item being sorted. Thus, in modes other than Synchronize Inputs, if all outputs through which a given type of item can be sent are blocked, tunnels that have received another item of that type block their inputs and cannot accept more items, but tunnels that have not received another item of that type (for example, tunnels that only receive a different item type) continue to accept input and deliver it to the proper (unblocked) outputs.

Combining Multiple Item Streams[]
Brass Tunnels can be used to combine items from different input streams forming a mixed output to one or more output portals. If there is only one output portal, then any value setting mode will work. If there are multiple outputs, then Prefer Nearest and Synchronize Inputs will not result in mixed outputs. 
A combination of tunnels and funnels can be used to create item streams with a particular ratio of item types. For example, forming brass ingots in a mixer requires an equal number of copper ingots and zinc ingots. This equal mix can be provided by feeding the copper and zinc ingots from individual chests through brass funnels set to the same stack size. The ingots are then fed by belt to two tunnels forming a group set to Synchronize Inputs. All outputs but one need to be filtered to reject copper and zinc ingots. The remaining output will have a properly balanced blend to feed into the mixer.

summary:

Contents

content:
The brass workshop, unsurprisingly, allows you to create Brass Ingots which opens up quite a lot of capabilities such as automated planting, item sorting, advanced redstone circuits, ore processors, and elevators. It requires access to the Nether to obtain a Blaze. 

Contents

1 Components
2 Layout
3 Power Source
4 Making Brass
5 Capabilities

5.1 Automated Planting
5.2 Item Sorting
5.3 Advanced Redstone Circuits
5.4 Ore Processing
5.5 Elevators





Components[]
The brass workshop builds off the Starter Workshop but adds a Blaze Burner for the heated mixing required to make brass. It also adds a belt mechanism to automate bulk processing of brass. The brass workshop requires no more rotational power than the starter workshop, so the power system remains the same with the exception of also driving the belt mechanism. 
The brass workshop has the following components:  

 Crafting Table
 Furnace
 Stonecutter
 Mechanical Press with  Depot
 Mechanical Mixer with  Basin
 Blaze Burner
 Hopper
 Andesite Funnel
 Chest x 5
Powering the mechanical press, mixer, and belt mechanism requires: 

2x  Water Wheel
4x  Cogwheel
3x  Large Cogwheel
2x  Gearbox
4x  Shaft
2x  Mechanical Belt
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Brass Workshop (front) 		 	 
Layout[]
The image "Brass Workshop (front)" shows an efficient layout. As with the starter workshop, it contains a mechanical mixer and a mechanical press. It adds a hopper to feed in recipe components, a belt feed to transport the mixer outputs and an andesite funnel to store the outputs in a chest.  The rectangular hole in the grass is there to show the belt mechanism. It can be filled in, except a space must be left open in front of the blaze burner to feed it fuel. 

Power Source[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Brass Workshop (back) 		 	 
The power source is described in detail in the Starter Workshop tutorial. This design adds only a few components to drive the belt that carries the brass ingots from the mixer basin to the chest. The image "Brass Workshop (back)" shows an extra shaft extending from the third large cogwheel. This shaft drives the vertical belt down to the gearbox which in turn drives the belt carrying the brass ingots.

Making Brass[]
Making brass is very simple with this workshop. Simply load two stacks of  Copper Ingots and two stacks of  Zinc Ingots to the hopper and feed a piece of  Coal or other fuel to the blaze burner. To automate larger production batches, add a chest on top of the hopper. This should produce about 25 brass ingots per minute and deposit them in the receiving chest. 
Note that you can still produce any other mixer recipe with this setup. This design is also great for bulk production of  Andesite Alloy.

Capabilities[]
Brass production opens up several new lines of capabilities in Create. 

Automated Planting[]
Create Brass Hands then Deployers to add automatic replanting to your crop and tree harvesting contraptions.

Item Sorting[]
Brass allows you to build Brass Tunnels, Brass Funnels, and Smart Chutes which, combined with mechanical belts and storage blocks, give great flexibility in sorting and routing items for production automation or sorted storage.

Advanced Redstone Circuits[]
Flatten brass ingots to make Pulse Timers, Pulse Extenders, and Pulse Repeaters. Among many other uses, these components can automatically trigger your crop and tree harvesting contraptions for unattended operation. 

Ore Processing[]
Bulk ore processing requires Crushing Wheels which require brass to create. Apply brass ingots to Stripped Logs to create Brass Casings. Combine the brass casings with an Electron Tube and a Crafting table to create Mechanical Crafters. Then use the mechanical crafters to build the crushing wheels. 

Elevators[]
Combine brass casings with Dried Kelp Blocks and Iron Sheets to make Elevator Pulleys.

Each Cardboard armor piece provides 1 () armor point, granting 4 () armor points in total.
While wearing a full set of armor, sneaking makes the player appear as a Cardboard Package and changes it's hitbox to be one block tall. Mobs cannot detect players in this state unless they are 1 block away.

Cardboard Packages are used to transport items through item networks.

Contents

1 Obtaining
2 Usage

2.1 Storage
2.2 Placement
2.3 Address

2.3.1 Glob




3 History



Obtaining[]
Cardboard Packages are created by a Packager. Their appearance is random.

Usage[]
Storage[]
Cardboard Packages can serve as temporary storage. They have 9 slots of inventory. They can be unpacked by shift-right-clicking, but this destroys the Cardboard Package.
When a storage block such as a Toolbox, Shulker Box, or Minecart Contraption is packaged, the Cardboard Package will only store one stack at a time.

Placement[]
Cardboard Packages can be placed in the world as entities either by right-clicking, dropping, or throwing them. Hold right-click to launch the package. The longer right-click is held, the greater the distance it is thrown.
Right click to pick them up again. Left click to unpack them and drop their contents.
A package is instantly unpacked when it comes in contact with Water.
The packages can also be unpacked by other sources of damage such as Mechanical Saws, Lava, or Cactus. 

Address[]
Cardboard Packages can be given an address to be delivered to on creation. Packages are labeled with an address on creation when the Packager receives a request through a Logistics Network, or when a Packager with a Sign is given a redstone signal. 
Packages will be sorted by their Address depending on matching addresses.
The following items have addresses:

 Package Filter
 Package Frogport
 Postbox
The following blocks can be used to request deliveries to an address:

 Redstone Requester
 Stock Ticker
 Factory Gauge
Glob[]
Create uses a glob (also known as a wildcard) to specify addresses for sorting. Globs are not as powerful as RegEx (regular expressions), but they are easier to learn.[1] The specific type of glob used by Create features:[2]

Regular character
Any non-special character matches only itself.
Escape character, Backslash \
Any special character can be turned into a regular character by prefixing it with backslash (\). This robs it of its special meaning. For example, \? matches the literal wuestion mark only. [Right Alt+Q]
Any-length wildcard, Asterisk *
Matches any substring, including empty ones.
1-length wildcard, Question mark ?
Matches exactly 1 of any character.
Character set, Brackets [chars]
Matches exactly 1 of any character in the set.
Negative character set, Bracket-bang [!chars]
Matches exactly 1 of any character not in the set.
Group, Braces {pat1,pat2}
Matches any of the subpatterns within, separated by a comma , from each
Examples of Glob usage are:




Glob
Description
Will match
Will not match


H*
matches any address that starts with H
Hero, Hero?brine!, H/arp
Notch, harm


*a
matches any address that ends with a
Aura, Enigma
Enigmatic


\*a
matches *a
*a
Aura


P??
matches any address that starts with P and is followed by 2 characters
Pat, Pea
Peat


????*
matches any address that has at least 4 characters
money, iron
dye


B[aeu]t
matches any address that starts with B, followed by a, e or u, followed by the last character, t
Bat, Bet
Bot, Bit


B[!aeu]t
matches any address that starts with B, followed by any character but a, e or u, followed by the last character, t
Bot, Bit
Bat, Bet


{Hello,Hi}
matches Hello or Hi
Hello, Hi
Aloha


{Farm,Mine}-Storage
matches Farm or Mine, followed by -Storage
Farm-Storage, Mine-Storage
Farm-Crusher


{Base1,Base2}-*
matches Base1 or Base2, followed by - and then anything
Base1-, Base2-Crusher
Base1


Base1{-*,}
matches Base1 or Base1 followed by - and then anything
Base1, Base1-, Base1-Crusher
Base2-Crusher

Globs are case-sensitive. Globs are internally translated to RegEx, but this does not mean you can use any real RegEx syntax.

Crafting[]

Cart Assembler

Any Log +Andesite Alloy +Redstone Dust





Usage[]
The Cart Assembler can be placed on Rails. When the assembler is powered with redstone, blocks placed on top of the assembler will be attached to minecarts that pass through it as a Contraption. Use Block Attachment Utilities to attach more blocks.





Rail Type

When Activated

When Deactivated


Rail

Assembles Cart Contraptions

Disassembles Cart Contraptions


Powered Rail

Assembles and releases Cart Contraptions

Disassembles and stops Cart Contraptions


Detector Rail

Assembles unassembled Cart Contraptions, Disassembles Assembled Cart Contraptions

N/A


Activator Rail

Disassembles Cart Contraptions. Unlike the other rails, the Cart Assembler is not required for this to happen.

N/A

Value Settings[]
The Value Settings Screen can be accessed on the side of the Cart Assembler to change the cart contraption's movement modes. 

Always face toward motion
Pause actors while rotating - Contraption Actors such as a Deployer will not work while the cart rotates.
Lock Rotation - the contraption will not change alignment along with the cart, and will retain the same rotation from when it was built, much like the effect of a Mechanical Bearing on a cart contraption.
Cart Contraptions[]
Similarly to rotating structures, having a Mechanical Bearing in the structure will cause the attached part to keep the same alignment as the cart moves.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Cart Contraptions made with a Furnace Minecart can automatically take Coal as fuel from onboard inventories.
Despite having collision with mobs or items, Cart Contraptions do not collide with blocks unless the appropriate world-interaction block makes the collision.
Cart contraptions will not travel through nether portals.

Item Form[]
Cart Contraptions can be taken into the inventory by right clicking them with a Wrench (Configurable.) Excluding entities, this keeps all storage and cart configuration. By default, if certain blocks are present on the Cart Contraption, such as Spawners or Budding Amethyst, the contraption cannot be picked up with a Wrench (Configurable.) By default, Cart Contraption items cannot be placed in inventories such as Shulker Boxes or Toolboxes (Configurable.)

Carriage Contraptions[]
Carriage contraptions are moving structures connected directly to two minecarts. 
Carriage Contraptions can be made by connecting two Cart Assemblers with minecarts using a structure. This will not work if the two minecarts are linked together by Minecart Coupling.
Carriage contraptions can also be disassembled by right clicking with a Wrench.
Aside from movement, there is no difference between the functions of a Carriage Contraption and a Single Cart Contraption. However, the smoother movement is better for moving mobs or items with only collision.

Minecarts with mounted contraptions can now be picked up as an item.
Furnace Minecarts can now be used in the Cart Assembler.
Fixed displaced coordinates between contraptions and their mounts to fix minecart contraptions disappearing when loaded near chunk borders.


0.2.4


Changed the way Cart Assemblers react to redstone input.
Fixed crash when assembled minecarts pick up the block below their assembler.


0.2.4b


Fixed server crash when Cart Assembler accelerates held Minecarts.


0.2.4d


Cart Assemblers now have several behaviours depending on the rail type they were placed on.


0.3


Contraptions can now be mounted between two Minecarts.
Chest Minecarts can now be used in the Cart Assembler.
Minecarts can no longer be moved while a contraption is stalling them.
Moved option input of cart assemblers to side faces.
Fixed activator rails not diassembling furnace minecart contraptions.
Fixed drills continuing to dig at old locations when placing a minecart structure somewhere else.
Cart contraptions now keep their item name.


0.3b


Cart Assemblers can now be placed on controller rails.


0.3c


Minecarts can now collide with non-mounted contraptions.


0.3.1


Fixed minecart contraptions started on a powered rail facing in unwanted directions.

Fixed minecart contraption items not facing away from the player when placed.
Fixed duplication of Cart Assemblers.


0.3.1c


Minecart Contraptions with exceeding NBT packet sizes can no longer be picked up.


0.3.2


Cart Assemblers now have a specific direction.
Assembled cart contraptions assemble and disassemble according to the assembler's direction.
Cart contraptions no longer turn exponentially.
Cart contraption now turn more sluggishly the larger they are.

Cart contraptions with attached Spawners can no longer be picked up with a Wrench (Configurable).
Fixed Mechanical Crafters duplicating and dropping their items when added to minecart contraption.
Fixed Wand Of Symmetry duplicating rails under placed Cart Assemblers.
Fixed Deployers not able to place down Cart Assemblers.
Add proper rotation and mirroring to CartAssemblerBlock.

Casings are blocks used throughout many crafting recipes in Create, as well as for decoration and aesthetic purposes.
There are four types of Casings: Andesite Casings are mainly used in basic contraptions, Brass Casings are used in more advanced machines, Copper Casings are strictly for fluids, and Train Casings for locomotive transportation.

Encasing[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Copper Casings can be used to prevent Pipes from connecting to each other. Note the casing over the three-way connection in the bottom image has isolated the top tank. 		 	 
Mechanical Belts, Shafts, and Cogwheels can be encased in most casings, creating a decoration around the encased block. Copper casings, however, can be used only on Fluid Pipes. Likewise, a fluid pipe will not accept any other kind of casing.

Although mostly decorative, casings can also be used to control multiple connections. Applying a casing to a pipe will prevent it from connecting to any additional pipes placed after the casing was applied, save for directly in front of the pipe opening. Casings on Cogwheels can prevent cogs from connecting to other cogs via the shaft. This allows cogs to be placed right next to each other without affecting each other. A Wrench applied to the face of the casing will toggle the shaft connection on and off.

The Chain Conveyor is used to transport Cardboard Packages. It has a secondary use of transferring rotational force across open spaces that aren't perfectly horizontal, vertical or on a 45° slope (where a Mechanical Belt would normally be used)

Usage[]
Placement[]
After placing a Chain Conveyor, they can be connected to other Chain Conveyors by right-clicking them with a Chain. The selection can be cleared by right-clicking the Chain Conveyor again. The Chain Conveyor requires 1 chain for every 
  
    
      
        2
        
          
            2
            3
          
        
      
    
    {\displaystyle 2{\frac {2}{3}}}
  
 blocks between the two Chain Conveyors. 
The maximum distance at which chain conveyors can be placed is 32 blocks, can add 8 blocks to the side if it is 32 blocks away (End and start is counted), and can be modified in config.  

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Maximum slope and placement distance of a Chain Conveyor 		 	 
The maximum angle at which chain conveyors can connect with elevation difference is 45°, plus an additional 2 blocks horizontal distance. The maximum distance at 45° slope is 23 blocks horizontal by 21 blocks vertical (center to center).  

Stress Network[]
Chain Conveyors can be used to transfer Kinetic Stress. As with normal Stress Network rules, the Stress Capacity of the network is added together and the rotation speed is taken to be the speed of the fastest-rotating unit. Also like other Stress-transferring components, the Chain Conveyor and/or the Chain connection breaks when a part of the network tries to contribute a rotational force in the opposite direction. The broken Conveyor and/or Chains drop as items.
Stress transfer does not require the intermediate chunks to be loaded. However, chain or conveyor breakage may happen over a long-distance network of Chain Conveyors due to chunk-loading ideosyncracies.

Transport[]
Riding the Chain[]
Right-click a Chain Conveyor with a Wrench to take a ride. Sneak to dismount. If the player right-clicks a chain while riding, the player is teleported to the target chain at the position of the right-click.
This can be the same chain or a different chain.
If the player collides with a block while riding, they will be thrown off.
When passing a Chain Conveyor, the player will be sent in the direction they’re looking towards. This can be an intersection or just a U-turn.

Packages[]
Main articles: Cardboard Package and Package Frogport
Cardboard Packages can be placed on Chain Conveyors via right-click. Package Frogports are used to automatically move Cardboard Packages from and to the Chain Conveyors. Chain Conveyors will automatically sort packages by their Address to send them to Frogports with a matching Address.

Charcoal is an item obtained by smelting logs or wood. It is used as fuel, or for crafting torches and campfires. Unlike coal, charcoal cannot be traded with villagers or crafted into a block of coal. Coal and charcoal also cannot stack together. It can be used as a substitute for coal, as both charcoal and coal have an equivalent duration when smelted.

Chromatic Compound is a material used to create Shadow Steel and Refined Radiance. It is also used to upgrade the Handheld Blockzapper.
Refined Radiance is created by dropping Chromatic Compound into a Beacon's light beam, or by dropping Chromatic Compound on the ground and surrounding it with light sources (which it will absorb). It is also worth noting that once it starts absorbing light and you pick it up, it shows a progress bar that looks the exact same as a durability bar which tells you how much more light is needed to become refined radiance
Shadow Steel is created by dropping a Chromatic Compound into the Void.

Chutes transport items vertically, generally downward unless an encased fan is used to blow items upward. There are two varieties: Chute and Smart Chute. Smart Chutes allow the player to control the types of items passed and their stack size.

Contents

Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Chute

Iron Sheet +  Iron Ingot

4



Smart Chute

Brass Sheet +Chute +Electron Tube





Usage[]
Transferring Items[]
Chutes can extract items from inventories or belts immediately above them and insert or deposit items on inventories or belts below them. Chutes will also collect items that fall upon them and will drop items into empty space if an inventory is not immediately below them. Chutes may be stacked either pure vertically or in a vertical diagonal to form a pipe for moving items. 
If the receiving inventory is full, chutes will hold one stack internally and stop accepting more items. Chutes cannot insert or extract items from the sides of inventories, although funnels may be used to insert or extract items from the sides of chutes. Chutes are limited to no more than 16 items in a stack while Smart Chutes can transport up to 64 items in a stack.

Hopper replacement[]
Since Create 6.0.7, Chutes can also insert compostable items into a Composter from the top, like a faster and cheaper version of the vanilla Hopper.[1] Because of how the Composter works, the Chute always inserts one item at a time. It does this by taking from the source (above) inventory a whole stack size, storing it inside the chute's internal stack, and transferring items down one-by-one in the internal stack. A Chute placed below can also extract the Bone Meal from the Composter.

Encased Fan Powered Chutes[]
Items in chutes will be affected by gravity and tumble downward by default. To push or pull items up, a powered Encased Fan is needed under or on top of the chutes respectively. For instance, a fan below the chutes would push items up and a fan above the chutes would pull items up. The speed of the Encased Fan can change how fast items go upwards.

Splitting & Merging[]
Multiple lines of chutes can merge into one, though the items will not merge into one stack. Without Smart Chutes, Fan powered chutes will initially prefer certain paths before overflowing into other lines if possible. Pushing Fan powered Chutes that split into multiple lines will prefer the straightest path. Pulling Fan powered chutes will draw the items to the powered fan. The airflow and the resulting item speed can increase or decrease as the Chutes merge and split, respectively.

Appearance[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			From left to right, a Chute, an encased Chute, and a Block of Industrial Iron. 		 	 
Chutes can be right clicked with a Wrench to be given windows.  Right clicking again removes the windows. Non-diagonal chutes can also be encased with Industrial Iron Blocks simply by clicking on the chute with an industrial iron block. The blocks are not consumed. To remove the industrial iron block appearance, simply click the chute with a wrench. Diagonal chutes already appear the same as encased Chutes.

Smart Chutes[]
Smart Chutes behave similarly to Brass Funnels. They can be filtered to only allow certain items through, configured to pass specific stack sizes (up to 64), and stopped with a redstone signal. Unlike funnels, they can insert and extract at the same time, but can only function vertically.
To restrict the Smart Chute to passing a single type of item, simply click the filter slot with the item. Clicking with a different item will change the filter to the new item. To remove a filter, click with an empty hand. Smart Chutes can also be configured to filter multiple item types by using a List or Attribute Filter. 
When directly below an inventory, the filter slot doubles as a Value Settings control, much like the Brass Funnel. The Chute can be adjusted to extract up to or exactly a set amount of items per stack. The Value Settings of a Smart Chute will be saved even when the inventory above is destroyed,

title: Circuits
summary: Create adds several components that can be used in redstone circuits. These include the Redstone Contact, Redstone Link, Linked Controller, Pulse Repeater, Pulse Extender, Pulse Timer, Powered Latch, and Powered Toggle Latch.  These components can make redstone circuits simpler and smaller as well a...
content:
Create adds several components that can be used in redstone circuits. These include the Redstone Contact, Redstone Link, Linked Controller, Pulse Repeater, Pulse Extender, Pulse Timer, Powered Latch, and Powered Toggle Latch.  These components can make redstone circuits simpler and smaller as well as giving finer control over timing.

Contents

1 Logic Gates

1.1 NOT GATE
1.2 AND, OR, NAND, and NOR Gates
1.3 XOR Gate


2 Clocks

2.1 Pulse Timer Clock
2.2 Pulse Repeater Clock
2.3 Variable Cycle Clock


3 Signal Comparators

3.1 Matching Signal-Strength Detector





Logic Gates[]
Logic gates are circuits that provide a digital output signal based on the conditions of one or more input signals. Digital signals are either on or off (powered or unpowered redstone) and usually represented as a 1 or 0 respectively. 

NOT GATE[]
The ability to place the Pulse Extender in an inverse output mode allows it to be used as a NOT gate. Simply set the pulse length to 2 ticks (or as needed for your particular circuit) and right click the Pulse Extender to toggle to inverse mode.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Extender NOT Gate 		 	 

A Powered Latch can also be used for a NOT gate. A continuously powered signal is sent to the set input and the control signal is sent to the reset input.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Powered Latch NOT Gate 		 	 
AND, OR, NAND, and NOR Gates[]
A simple pattern of three Pulse Extenders can act as an AND, OR, NAND, or NOR gate depending only on the selection of inverse settings among the Pulse Extenders. If we label the two input Pulse Extenders A and B, and the output O, then the following table shows the Normal (N) versus Inverse (I) setting of each Pulse Extender to achieve the indicated gate. (Note that there are smaller circuit options for some of the gates.)






Pulse Extender Inversion Settings


GATE

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Extender AND Gate 		 	 

XOR Gate[]
Pulse Extenders can be used to create a single layer XOR Gate. The design shown below uses repeaters to push charges into opaque blocks which act as diodes providing isolated signals to both the redstone dust continuing to the right and the redstone dust between the two blocks. The center Pulse Extender injects an inverted signal into another block which also acts as an isolating diode forming independent OR Gates with the redstone dust on the far side and near side of the block. All three of the Pulse Extenders are in the inverted mode.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Extender XOR Gate 		 	 
Clocks[]
Pulse Timer Clock[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Timer 		 	 
The Pulse Timer is itself a clock. It repeatedly emits a short pulse with a user-set delay between pulses. Note that the short pulse may not be long enough to have the desired effect (such as starting a minecart with a powered rail). In this case, place a Redstone Repeater or a Pulse extender between the pulse timer and the item to be powered.
Clicking on the pulse timer inverts the output signal. Applying a redstone signal to the side of the pulse timer with the small triangle will inhibit the pulse.

Pulse Repeater Clock[]
A Pulse Repeater along with a Redstone Repeater can make a pulse clock where a short pulse is repeatedly sent out with a selectable delay between pulses.  In the clock shown below, the Redstone Repeater must have at least 1 tick delay. A pulse input on any of the redstone lines will start the clock. Note that the pulse from a button is too long and will interfere with the feedback signal from the repeater. To start the clock, you can quickly switch a lever on and off or you can feed a button output through another Pulse Repeater set to 2 ticks. The delay between pulses is controlled by the delay setting on the Pulse Repeater.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Repeater Clock 		 	 


Variable Cycle Clock[]
Two pulse extenders, one in inverse mode, can make a clock with independently settable on and off durations. The clock will start itself when one of the two pulse extenders is set to inverse mode.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Variable Cycle Pulse Extender Clock 		 	 
Signal Comparators[]
Signal comparators compare the strength of two input signals from which they output a signal based on the similarity or difference in the two input signals. 

Matching Signal-Strength Detector[]
A matching signal-strength detector emits a signal when the strengths of two input signals are equal. When the input signals are unequal, the detector output is off. 
The circuit shown below will detect matching signal strengths between 1 and 15. In this circuit, the comparator on the right is in subtraction mode, causing it to subtract the strength of the signal entering the side from the strength of the signal entering the base. The circuit will trigger an output signal when the output of the comparator on the right is of strength one. This means the left side signal must be reduced by one, which is done here by the string of two redstone dust. 

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Matching Strength Detector 		 	 
The output of the subtraction comparator is fed to a pulse extender acting as an inverter and a repeater acting as a one-way diode. The output of these two devices is ORed then input to another pulse extender acting as an inverter. The circuit output will be ON only when the outputs of both the pulse extender and the repeater are off. This condition will occur only when the output power of the subtraction comparator is exactly one, powering the pulse extender inverter but not the repeater.
If the strength of the side signal is greater than the base signal, the subtraction will be negative. The comparator will put out no signal. The pulse extender inverter will therefore output a signal which then turns off the circuit's final output.  If the strength of the side signal is less than the base signal, then the subtraction comparator will put out a signal strength of at least two, thus ensuring that both the pulse extender inverter and the repeater are powered. In this case, the signal from the repeater turns off the circuit's final output.
This simple circuit will not detect matching strengths of zero. Also, if the left signal is zero and the right signal is one, the circuit will give a false positive result. Care must be taken that the left side signal never be less than one.
One use for a matching strength detector is to create a combination lock. Only when a player sets the proper signal strength will a desired action occur. Multiple circuits can be ORed together prior to the final inverter to create a multi-digit combination lock.

Usage[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			A Clipboard with a Schematicannon Checklist. 		 	 
Use a clipboard in hand or use a placed clipboard to access its interface. Items on the checklist can be written out or checked off, or all checked items can be erased.

Placement[]
Sneak use a clipboard to place it on the ground. Sneak use it again or break it to pick it up.

Copying and Pasting[]
Use the clipboard on a block with Value Settings to copy them, such as a Brass Funnel or a Mechanical Bearing, then left click another to paste them. When pasting a setting including a filter, having a filter in the inventory will be required to paste the setting.
Clicking a placed Clipboard with an item Clipboard will add the placed Clipboard's entries onto the item Clipboard's entries. This will not allow duplicate entries.

Schematicannon[]
Put the Clipboard in a ready Schematicannon to get the Schematicannon's Checklist. Like with a Book and Quill, the Clipboard's checklist can be updated by putting it in the Schematicannon again. Items can also be checked off manually. Once finished with the Schematicannon's checklist, the Clipboard can be blanked again by either using the "Erase checked items" option, or putting it through the Crafting Grid.

Displaying Text[]
A clipboard can also paste text written in it to a Display Board or Nixie Tubes. Nixie Tubes will only take text from the Clipboard's first bullet point, whereas Display Boards will attempt to display all of a Clipboard's points from the Clipboard's selected page. Pasting text onto a Display Board from a Clipboard works much like using a Name Tag on it.

Addresses[]
Addresses can be saved to the Clipboard by right-clicking a Package Frogport or Postbox. They can also be added manually by typing the desired address with a # at the beginning.
This allows the clipboard to suggest and autofill Addresses in relevant GUIs when in the player's inventory or placed within 32 blocks of the player. 
Clicking the addresses in the clipboard's GUI disables them and prevents them from showing up as a suggestion. They can be re enabled by clicking them again. Disabled addresses count as "checked," and will be deleted when erasing checked items.

The Cogwheel is a basic mechanical component in Create that relays rotation.
The Large Cogwheel is a larger variant of the cogwheel that can relay rotation around corners and power Rotation Speed Controllers.

Usage[]
Conveying Rotation[]
 	https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Cogwheel_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scenes for a Cogwheel. 		 	 
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Two seperated cogwheels 		 	 
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Two seperated large cogwheels 		 	 
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Diagonally connected cogwheel and large cogwheel 		 	 
Cogwheels have three main methods of interlocking:

Two Cogwheels interlock when placed next to each other (not diagonally) and facing the same direction. When rotational force is provided to one of the cogwheels, the force will be provided to the other Cogwheel at the same speed but in the opposite direction.
Two Large Cogwheels interlock when placed perpendicular to each other, effectively changing its axis and direction, but not its speed.
A Cogwheel and a Large Cogwheel interlock when placed diagonally to each other and facing the same direction. The Large Cogwheel will rotate at half the speed of the Cogwheel.
A cogwheel can also be used like a Shaft, conveying rotation from the ends of its axis. They can be stopped from doing this by applying a Casing, configurable with a Wrench. Mechanical components can be connected to each end, and several Cogwheels connected end-to-end function the same as multiple shafts would.

RPM Enhancing Rigs[]
 	https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Cogwheel_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Using pairs of Cogwheels and Large Cogwheels, rotational speed can be easily doubled or halved using the mechanic mentioned above. It is possible to connect many pairs of Large Cogwheels and Cogwheels to apply this mechanic repeatedly, up to 256 RPM (Though that limit can be increased or decreased in the Config).
A Large Cogwheel can also be connected to a Rotation Speed Controller, to adjust speed more precisely.

Activating Components[]
Some blocks need to be powered by a Cogwheel to function. Those blocks contain a Cogwheel in their texture and can be powered by placing a Cogwheel adjacent to them or a large Cogwheel diagonally, both in the same direction as the block, like a normal Cogwheel.
Components that can only be powered by cogwheels :

 Display Board
 Mechanical Arm
 Mechanical Crafter
 Mechanical Mixer
 Millstone does not have a Shaft on the bottom side)

Conductors are special passive mobs in Create:Steam 'n' rails. 

They can be constructed by placing any conductor hat on an andesite casing; they can also be made using deployers. 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Conductor wearing a red conductor cap 		 	 
Conductor will wear the conductor cap you used to make them.
Uses of the Conductor
Conductors can be used to transport toolboxes by right clicking them but they cannot walk by themselves so you need to right click them with lead to make them follow you around if you wish to remove the toolbox sneak click the conductor.
Conductors can pull levers and push buttons by looking at them, if you put buttons and levers all around they can only press one button/lever randomly. If you are wearing a hat that is different from the conductor's hat the conductor is currently wearing they will not respond.
Upon right-click, a conductor can be given Engineer's Goggles. Then, you can bind a remote lens to that conductor by right-clicking it with the lens. Bound conductors can share their point of view in a camera-like screen when the bound remote lens is right-clicked in the air. It is also possible to move around as the conductor in this mode. Press shift to exit.
Conductor Whistle
The conductor whistle can be used to call the train anywhere on the track. Right click a seated conductor acting as a train controller with a conductor whistle to bind the whistle to that train. Right clicking the track will call the train to that spot on the track. Right clicking a station with the whistle will call the train to the station.
Conductor whistles work with deployers on train stations and also with tracks (with exceptions). A deployer used on a train station with the whistle will work as normal. A deployer used on a track with a whistle will automatically call the train in the positive direction of that coordinate. This means that trains can only be called to move in the +x or +z directions with deployers on tracks.
Redstone Controlled Conductors/Trains
Right clicking the conductor with a redstone link will make the conductor redstone controllable and is indicated by a redstone receiver being added to its hat. To control the conductor, set the frequencies you want for the conductor on a linked controller and right click the conductor with the linked controller (there is no indicator for this). You should now be able to use the linked controller to move the conductor around.
The frequencies set in the linked controller that you right clicked the conductor with will be stored in the conductor. For example: if you set the frequency for "forward" using stone in red and wood in blue on your linked controller and right clicked the conductor with it, you can now make the conductor move forward by placing down a redstone link with stone in red and wood in blue and powering it.
If the conductor is seated and controlling a train, you can use redstone links or linked controllers to drive the train remotely. Holding "shift" or "space" will make the train move and stop at the next station. If the train isn't moving, holding "shift" or "space" and pressing in the direction you want to go will make the train go to the station in that direction.
As of the latest update, the conductor cannot reverse trains through redstone control, even if it has access to both train controls. It can still travel to stations in the reverse direction by holding "shift" or "space" and pressing reverse but freely controlling it in reverse is not possible at the moment.

Create mod has multiple config options that can be used to adjust the Create experience. These settings can be changed in-game at any time through the pause or title screen menu. 
They are also located in 3 folders: create-client.toml, create-common.toml, and create-server.toml. Keep in mind the server file is located in each world save rather than in the config folder.

Obtaining[]
Contraptions can be made by using Movement Anchors such as:

 Mechanical Piston
 Cart Assembler
 Gantry Carriage
 Mechanical Bearing
 Windmill Bearing
 Clockwork Bearing
 Rope Pulley
 Elevator Pulley
 Trains
Usage[]
Creation[]
Assembly and Disassembly[]
Contraptions are created when a Movement Anchor is activated and the attached blocks are assembled into a Contraption. Most Movement Anchors will activate when given Rotational Force and disassemble back into blocks when not receiving power or when the Contraption is unable to move. Others are activated manually or by Redstone. Most anchors have Movement Modes that change the conditions for when they disassemble.

Attaching Blocks[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			A Mechanical Bearing on a Mechanical Bearing Contraption. 		 	 
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			A minecart contraption with a Mechanical Bearing. 		 	 
Each Movement Anchor has at least one sticky side and can move at least one block with no extra utilities. Multiple blocks can be moved with the use of Block Attachment Utilities such as:

 Linear Chassis
 Radial Chassis
 Super Glue
 Sticker
 Slime Block
 Honey Block
Blocks that attach to other blocks, such as Levers, Signs, or Torches, will automatically become part of the Contraption. Blocks that automatically attach to other blocks of the same type, such as Sails, Piston Extension Poles, Mechanical Belts, and Gantry Shafts, only need to be glued in one place.
Blocks can stick to sticky chassis, but chassis won't stick to blocks on their own. Slime Blocks on Contraptions will not pick up Honey Blocks and vice versa, and neither will pick up Glazed Terracotta. They will still pick up other blocks such as Furnaces.
A Mechanical Bearing can be added to a Contraption to attach a second Contraption that keeps one alignment as the structure moves. It can be attached at any orientation.

Unmovable Blocks[]
Certain blocks cannot be moved by Contraptions by default. Other blocks can be moved, but when on Minecart Contraptions, the cart cannot be picked up with a Wrench. For certain blocks, this is adjustable in the config. Movement Anchors are also unmovable while they are active.

Movement Modes[]
Most Movement Anchors have movement modes that can be changed through their Value Settings Screen by hovering over their side and holding right-click to access the interface. Most anchors include "Always place when stopped," "Only place near starting position," and "Only place when anchor is destroyed," determining when the blocks are placed back into the world. Cart Assemblers have "always face movement," "pause actors while rotating," and "lock rotation."

Collision[]
Gantry Carriages, Rope Pulleys, and Mechanical Pistons will stop moving if an unmovable block or set of blocks is in their path. Trains, Cart Assembler Contraptions, Elevator Pulleys, and Bearings will only collide with blocks if the appropriate world interaction block makes the collision.
Entities will also collide with Contraptions.

Items[]
 Copper Ingot - An item created by smelting copper ore or crushed copper ore or killing drowned.
 Crushed Copper Ore - An item obtained by crushing copper ore or copper blocks. Can be smelted into copper ingots or washed into copper nuggets.
 Copper Nugget - An item that can be crafted into a copper ingot.
 Copper Sheet - An item created by pressing a copper ingot.
Blocks[]
 Copper Ore - An ore found underground. Can be smelted into copper ingots or crushed into crushed copper ore.
 Copper Casing - A block created with wood and copper ingots. Can be used to craft fluid components.
 Block of Copper - A block used for compact copper storage and to create the base/pyramid for a Beacon.
 Copper Shingles - A decorative block crafted from copper sheets.
 Copper Tiles - A decorative block crafted from copper shingles.
 Copper Valve Handle - A slower, more precise version of the Hand Crank.
 Fluid Pipe - A block used to transfer fluids.
 Mechanical Pump - A block used to move fluids along pipes.
 Smart Fluid Pipe - A block used to filter fluids.
 Fluid Valve - A block used to control the flow of fluids.
 Fluid Tank - A block used to store fluids.
 Portable Fluid Interface - A block used to transfer fluids to and from moving contraptions.
 Spout - A block used to fill fluid container items and for certain recipes which require fluids.
 Hose Pulley - A block used to place or drain fluids.
 Item Drain - A block used to empty fluid container items.

Usage and How to fill[]
When placed, the backtank can be filled with air via Rotational Force. Simply attach a rotating Shaft to the Shaft at the top of the tank. When worn it provides 4 () armor points. Currently, it is only used with the Extendo Grip, Diving Helmet, and Potato Cannon. 
When used with the Diving Helmet it can provide up to 15 minutes of Water Breathing if not enchanted with the capacity enchantment. With Capacity III, it can provide 30 minutes of Water Breathing. It cannot be used with a chestplate, as it uses the chest slot in the inventory.
The player will receive a warning when the Backtank reaches 10% and 0% capacity.

Before Create 6.0.0, Create's copper looked a lot different, and there was a texture pack to make vanilla copper match it. Unfortunately, the release of Create 6.0.0, the textures were changed to match vanilla copper. If you preferred the look of Create's copper, there is a texture pack that changes it back that you can find right here. You can also pair the pack with this to make more vanilla copper blocks and items match.

Copper Ore is a Mineral block found underground. It can be processed into copper ingots which are used in a variety of recipes within the mod.

Contents

1 Obtaining
2 Usage
3 Trivia
4 History



Obtaining[]
Copper ore can be found between y=40 and y=85, and can be found in abundance around y=50.

Usage[]
 Crushed Copper Ore - An item obtained by crushing copper ore or copper blocks. Can be smelted into copper ingots or washed into copper nuggets.
 Copper Nugget - An item that can be crafted into a copper ingot.
Trivia[]
Copper Ore slowly turns a bluey-green over time, this is to reflect real life 'Oxidation'.
The in-game mechanics of this relies of random ticks to oxidize, like crops, it will not change out of the 'random tick' range.
