Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Mechanical Belt

Dried Kelp





Usage[]
Placement[]
Placing a Belt requires at least two Shafts. Place the Belt by right-clicking on the first shaft and then right clicking the second. Regardless of the length, this only consumes one mechanical belt. Both shafts must face the same direction.
A Mechanical Belt can be placed over any number of Shafts arranged horizontally, vertically, or diagonally (45° towards the y axis) in a single line, provided that no obstructions are present and that the total length is no longer than twenty blocks (adjustable in the Config). The Mechanical Belt also requires that the two shafts face the same direction. Andesite Casings and Brass Casings can be placed over any segment of a Belt.
Once a Belt is placed, it can be extended by right clicking the end with a Mechanical Belt in hand while the belt is under 20 blocks, though this does not consume the belt. Belts can also be shortened by right clicking them with a Wrench. Both actions relocate the Shaft.

Moving Entities and Items[]
The Mechanical Belt can transport items from one location to another. Items can either be thrown onto the belt or machines such as Funnels, Chutes and Mechanical Arms can place items onto the belt or remove items from the belt. A belt can also transport entities and the player. Diving Boots can be worn to negate this effect. You can also negate it while crouching. Items cannot be moved by vertical belts. The belt moves items at

If you need to transport more than 600 items per minute, you will need to use a Brass Funnel to place stacks of items on the belt. At 64 RPM, this results in a throughput of 9600 items/min.

Relaying Rotational Power[]
When rotational force is connected to any shaft of a belt, the belt conveys identical force to every other shaft it is connected to. As such, if two shafts are connected to external sources of rotational force, a belt cannot be placed connecting them unless the force is in the same direction and at the same speed.

Interaction[]
Components that are commonly used in conjunction with the Mechanical Belt include:

 Mechanical Press
 Deployer
 Spout
 Brass Tunnel
 Funnel
 Chute
 Depot
 Mechanical Arm
 Encased Fan
A Mechanical Press presses items on the belt that pass underneath it. Deployers can use their held item on the items that are on the belt which is useful for making train tracks and precision mechanisms. Spouts also fills valid items with the corresponding liquid that it has been supplied with. Brass Tunnels may be used to separate items from stacks or reorganize them as they move along the belt and through the Brass Tunnels. Chutes and Funnels can place items from machine inventories onto the belt or take items off the belt when facing the belt. A belt can place items onto a Depot which allows other machines such as a Chute or a Mechanical Arm to pick up the item and transfer them somewhere else. Encased Fans can modify the item on the belt as it travels along it such as bulk washing or bulk smelting. 

Dyeing[]
Mechanical Belts can be dyed be right clicking on them with a Dye. This will add colored stripes along the edges of the belt. To remove the dye, right click on the belt with a Water Bucket or Water Bottle.

Usage[]
Setup[]
Right click the front of a Mechanical Crafter with a Wrench to change the direction it sends items during crafting. The Mechanical Crafters are only connected by this path.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Mechanical crafter setup, with added arrows showing required blocks orientation to set up successfully. Also note the cog used to operate the crafter setup. 		 	 
Mechanical Crafters can be automatically filled by Funnels or Hoppers. 
On the back and sides of Mechanical Crafters, a Wrench can be used to connect or disconnect the inventory of two adjacent crafters. Crafters can share inventories while not participating in the same crafting recipe.
Items can also be inserted or removed by hand.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Mechanical crafter piece, with added arrow showing orientation as indicated by the block design 		 	 
Power[]
Each Mechanical Crafter has an internal gear that can only be powered by adjacent Mechanical Crafters or any size Cogwheel. This means only 1 Mechanical Crafter in a setup needs to be powered by a Cogwheel.

Auto-Crafting[]
When powered by rotational force and either powered with Redstone or all crafter slots are filled, Mechanical Crafters will send their items to adjacent crafters. For a successful recipe, the items must eventually meet in one crafter. Once all of the items reach the final Crafter, they will turn into the product. Crafters with Crafter Slot Covers act as empty spaces in a recipe; they can also be used to connect the inventory of otherwise separate crafters. Crafter Slot Covers will not move as recipe items will.
Powered Mechanical Crafters will start crafting once every Mechanical Crafter has been filled, or when they receive a redstone signal.
Mechanical Crafters are able to assemble invalid crafting recipes, but will eject the items once they are together instead of turning them into the crafting product.

Automating Crafting[]
Directly adjacent slots can be merged. This means that recipes that involve a block or ring of one material, such as andesite alloy, will hold only that one item type. The material can then be fed in via a hopper from the side.



 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			A crafter setup crafting a Mechanical Arm. You can tell which crafters share inventories and which do not by the borders. The crafters along the bottom allow one hopper to provide both with the ingredients. 		 	 
Output[]
Once a recipe is assembled in the final Crafter, the item will either be placed into the inventory of the block the Crafter's path sends items to, or will be ejected into the world  at that side of the Crafter if no such block exists.
If the final Crafter directs the finished product back into the recipe, the item must be manually removed from the Crafters by a player.

Mechanical Crafting Exclusive Recipes[]
Certain recipes cannot be crafted with regular Crafting tables and require the use of Mechanical Crafters. Those recipes include:

Wrench[]
Shift-right-clicking on a Mechanical Drill with a Wrench will destroy the Mechanical Drill and place it in your inventory.

Usage[]
Breaking Blocks[]
A stationary Mechanical Drill will break blocks in the block in front of it with a time in seconds of (45 x Hardness)/RPM and will hurt entities in an area around it.

A Mechanical Drill moved by Contraptions will break blocks and damage entities with which it collides without needing a direct supply of Rotational Force. 
The time it takes for a Mechanical Drill to break a block is based on the Contraption's speed and the block's Hardness value. The damage dealt to entities is also based on the Contraption's speed.

Cobblestone farm[]
The Mechanical Drill can be easily used to make a cobblestone farm fully automatic.

Obtaining[]

Name

Recipe




Mechanical Harvester
Andesite Alloy +  Iron Sheet +  Andesite Casing



Usage[]
Harvesting[]
The Mechanical Harvester will harvest all mature crops it comes in contact with while moving forward. (Enabling the config option Harvest Partially Grown will make the Mechanical Harvester harvest ALL crops, mature or not.) It will then either deposit the items to an inventory on the Contraption or, if no inventories are available, it will drop the items on to the ground. After harvesting, the plants will be reset to their initial growth state. (Disabling Harvester Replants in the config will instead reset the farmland to contain no crops.)
Unlike most components, the Mechanical Harvester cannot be powered while stationary. This is likely due to the fact that in order for the Harvester to work, it must be within the same block as the mature crop to harvest, which could not happen with a stationary component.
Harvesters can harvest and re-plant:

Wheat
Potatoes
Carrots
Beetroot
Cocoa Beans
Nether wart
Melon stems (for 0-2 melon seeds)
Pumpkin stems (for 0-2 pumpkin seeds)
Harvesters can break:

Sugar cane
Kelp
Any flower including torchflower except spore blossom
Pitcher plant
Any grass including seagrass, crimson/warped roots and nether sprouts
Any fern
Dead bush
Any sapling
Any small mushroom
Twisting, warped and cave vines
Small dripleaf
Any leaves (and drop the leaves block)
Harvesters can harvest sweet berries from sweet berry bushes.
Cactus blocks cannot be harvested and must be collected using a Mechanical Saw instead.

In-Game Description[]
"A mechanical plant cutter suitable for large to small scale crop automation. It is movable with Mechanical Pistons, Bearings or other controllers."

Obtaining[]
Breaking[]
Mechanical Mixer can be mined using any pickaxe. If mined without a pickaxe, it drops nothing.

Usage[]
The Mechanical Mixer is powered by an internal cogwheel, and will behave as one to any adjacent components, relaying and reversing rotation sideways.
The Mixer requires a minimum rotational speed of 30 RPM from its power source to work. Mixers will process ingredients faster the more speed it is given.
To work, a Mixer must be placed directly above a Basin, with a 1 block gap. When a valid recipe is inserted by throwing the ingredients in the Mixer, the Mixer will automatically combine the ingredients.

All shapeless crafting recipes can be made automatically using the Mechanical Mixer by inserting required items into the Basin under the mixer. An example of such recipe is:

Automating Brewing[]
All Brewing recipes can be made automatically using the Mechanical Mixer by inserting the required items and fluids into the Basin under the mixer. Brewing recipes require heating with a blaze burner.

Usage[]
Mechanical Pistons are a Contraption that will collide with unmovable blocks.

Moving Blocks[]
To extend, the Piston must have Piston Extension Poles at the end as well as Rotational power. The maximum extension pole length is 64 blocks, and this can be changed in the Config.
When the rotation is reversed, the piston will retract. The end must be made sticky with a Slimeball to bring the pushed blocks back with it.
A placed Mechanical Piston can be made sticky by right-clicking it with a Slimeball.
Multiple blocks can be pushed with the use of Block Attachment Utilities.

Usage[]
Placement[]
The Plough can only be placed on the horizontal face of a solid block, however, this block is not necessary to support the Plough after it is placed.

Breaking Blocks[]
While attached to a Contraption, the Mechanical Plough will break non-collidable blocks it comes in contact with (ex. snow layers).

Tilling[]
While attached to a Contraption, the Mechanical Plough will till any grass blocks below it (change grass blocks to farmland), which can be used to quickly till huge farms.

Flinging Entities[]
While attached to a Contraption that moves the Mechanical Plough in a swinging motion, any colliding entities will be flung in the direction of the swing.

The Mechanical Press is a mechanical component that applies Pressing, Packing, and Compacting recipes to items below it. It is an important early-game item, as it is used to press Ingots into Sheets, which are important ingredients for higher-level components.
The Mechanical Press is powered by an internal Shaft, accessed from two opposite sides. Much like Shafts, Presses will relay rotation along their axis. It processes items faster when it receives faster rotational power.

Obtaining[]
Crafting[]

Ingredients

Mechanical Press

Shaft +Andesite Casing +Block of Iron





Usage[]
Pressing[]
By default, the Mechanical Press will apply Pressing recipes to items underneath it. This can be set up in two ways: 

When placed one space above any block, it will process all valid items on the block when given rotational power. Items with no pressing recipe are unaffected.
When placed one space above a Mechanical Belt, it will automatically press incoming items, stalling the belt until each operation is done. Items with no pressing recipe are ignored.
Pressing recipes cannot be applied in bulk (unless you change the Config.)

Packing[]
When a Mechanical Press is placed above a Basin, it will apply Packing or Compacting recipes to ingredients in the Basin. Packing and Compacting recipes are applied one at a time and cannot be applied in bulk.
Packing recipes are any 2x2 or 3x3 crafting recipe that uses the same item in every slot. Some examples are:

The Mechanical Press will begin packing items as soon as there are enough of the same item.

Compacting[]
When a Mechanical Press is placed above a Basin, it will apply Packing or Compacting recipes to ingredients in the Basin. Packing and Compacting recipes are applied one at a time and cannot be applied in bulk. Compacting recipes are following:

Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Mechanical Pump

Cogwheel +Fluid Pipe




Usage[]
Mechanical Pumps (MPs) have a maximum range of 16 blocks (configurable) on either side, though this does not seem to apply to pipes themselves. You may however have up to 30 pipes between pumps. Mechanical Pumps will move fluid in only one direction at a time. 
The Brown arrow symbols on the pump indicate the direction of flow. The flow direction can be changed by using a Wrench. When a wrench is used, the entire valve will appear to have rotated 180 degrees. The brown directional arrows will appear on the other side of the pump's gear.
Mechanical pumps transfer fluid at the base rate of 
  
    
      
        Q
        =
        
          
            n
            2
          
        
      
    
    {\displaystyle Q={\frac {n}{2}}}
  
, where Q is the rate in mB/t and n is the rotational speed in RPM. Thus, Mechanical Pumps at a higher rotational speed will transfer fluids faster.

Advanced usage[]
The pipes actually do conform to the 16-block rule, but it requires a rephrasing of the range mechanism: the Mechanical Pump (MP) can go forward or backward for a range of 16 (configurable) blocks for a valid fluid port, which can be:

A pipe end exposed to air or a waterloggable block
A pipe end exposed to a drainable fluid
Any fluid container (Fluid Tank, Cauldron, etc.)
Another MP running in the same direction as itself
A pipe that is out of range of this MP, but is driven by another MP running in the same direction as this MP
The actual fluid transfer rates are derived from the base rate of the MP(s) in the network through a set of (seemingly innocuous) rules that operate on the branching pattern of the pipes leading up to input ports as outlined in Fluid Pipe § Fluid Transfer Rates. However, unintuitive behavior arises easily and clever use of the rules leads to total transfer rates exceeding the base rate (it is possible to gain 59× the base rate from 9 MPs). The rules require several pictures to explain; for now readers are advised to use a machine translator on the corresponding mcmod.cn article.[1]
When two MPs for the same direction are connected end-to-end (in series), the downstream MP directly inherits the transfer rate of the upstream MP. As a result, it is possible to save Stress by driving the downstream pump slower without affecting transfer rates.
When two MPs for the same direction are connected side-by-side (in parallel), the output rate is a sum of their two transfer rates. This can be rationalized through the aforementioned rules about ports and pipes, as the mcmod.cn article has demonstrated.

Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Mechanical Roller
Electron Tube +  Andesite Casing +  Crushing Wheel



Usage[]
Placement[]
When attempting to place the Roller on the top face of a block, it will be placed one block above it, similarly to a Mechanical Mixer or Mechanical Press. Though it appears to take up a few blocks of space, it only takes up one. There is also Placement Assist functionality, allowing for easy placement of Rollers to either of two sides of a roller. The Roller can be picked up by sneak using a Wrench on it.

Value Settings[]
The Mechanical Roller has three modes:

Clear Blocks and Pave - The Mechanical Roller will break blocks in front of it at its own level, as well as one level below it. If its Filter is set, it will also break blocks one level below that, replacing them with the block in the Filter. The roller will not harvest blocks that require a stone tool or higher, and otherwise has a chance to void blocks it harvests.
Straight Fill Below - The Roller will not break blocks, but will place blocks defined by its Filter straight below itself in available spaces as it moves.
Sloped Fill Below - The Roller will not break blocks, but will place blocks defined by its Filter below it sloping outward in available spaces as it moves.
Filtering[]
The Mechanical Roller's filter will accept any block that is not a Stair block, Entity Block, or lacks collision. Adjacent Rollers will copy other Roller's filters, even if they are placed later.

Placing & Breaking[]
The Mechanical Roller functions when moved horizontally toward the direction its facing. When moved to the side or up and down, it does not break or place blocks. When given Slabs as a filter, the Roller will place double slab blocks.
The Roller can place blocks up to 12 blocks below itself by default (Configurable.)
The roller will not break Train Tracks or blocks with little collision, such as Cobwebs or Saplings. The Roller has a chance to void everything it harvests(you can expect around a 50% void rate), and will always void blocks that require a Stone Tool or higher to be harvested.
When a Roller is at slab height and the block defined by its Filter has slab variants, it will start placing them, even if none are present in the contraption's inventory. This is most common when the Roller is on a Train going up a slope. When this happens, it will also place a full block underneath each slab.

Damage[]
Entities caught under a moving Roller will receive damage based on the Roller's speed if applicable, similar to Mechanical Saws or Mechanical Drills.

Usage[]
Chopping[]
Mechanical Saws are powered through rotational force, and when placed down facing to the side they will automatically chop down wood blocks in front of them. When chopping down a tree or giant mushroom, it will automatically destroy the entire tree by only destroying the bottom-most block. Blocks tagged as TREE_ATTACHMENTS will also be broken if found on the tree.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			the 2x2 tree in this setup will be cut down wholly 		 	 
Mechanical saws are only supposed to mine 2x2 trees as long as at least the last block (horizontally) is mined using the saw. The easiest way to bypass this is by removing the block immediately above the block being cut, in which case the entire 2x2 tree will be cut down by the mechanical saw.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			this setup will not be mined wholly, only one block in front of the mechanical saw is mined instead 		 	 
Mechanical saws can mine any structure of logs that doesn't have a vertical 2x2 square with the block being destroyed as one of the bottom blocks
Mechanical saws are automatically powered when on a create Contraption. The saw will damage entities and break blocks at a certain speed depending on the contraption's speed.
Mechanical saws can break the following blocks directly:

Any logs (including stripped logs)
Any wood (including stripped wood)
Any leaves
Non-muddy mangrove roots
Mushroom stems
Cactus blocks
Bamboo
Pumpkins and Melons
Mangrove roots can be broken like logs but do not count as a log to leaves
Mechanical saws can break non-stem mushroom blocks and wart blocks when they are connected to the block directly broken and there is another log/wood/stripped log/stripped wood/mangrove roots block adjacent to or above the block directly broken.
Leaves can be broken by being placed directly in front of a saw. They can serve as the first block broken in a tree if there is a log adjacent to or above it. Leaves will only be broken if the number of blocks it takes to connect it to the block broken is equal to or less than the number of blocks it takes to connect it to another log, if it can be connected to another log/wood/stripped log/stripped wood block by those or other leaves

Sawing[]
When placed facing upward, the Saw applies sawing or stonecutting recipes. When a recipe has multiple outputs, an output will be randomly selected unless a filter is applied to the Filter slot located next to the saw blade.

content:
Although automated Melon and Pumpkin farms can be made in vanilla Minecraft, Create makes them much easier to build. And Create can automatically craft Melon Slices back into whole melons for trading.

Contents

1 Compact Melon and Pumpkin Farm

1.1 Balancing Production
1.2 Items Needed
1.3 Building the Farm
1.4 Rail Line
1.5 Harvesting Contraption
1.6 Setting a Timer
1.7 Crafting Whole Melons

1.7.1 Building the Short Belt
1.7.2 Building the Crafter
1.7.3 Building the Bypass Belt
1.7.4 Installing the Item Handling Components


1.8 Power Source
1.9 Operating the Farm





Compact Melon and Pumpkin Farm[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Compact Melon and Pumpkin Farm 		 	 
This design produces a very efficient farm that can be extended in length and tiled in width. This tutorial will create a balanced production of whole Melons and Pumpkins.  

Balancing Production[]
Pumpkins harvest whole. Melons harvest as Melon Slices which must be crafted together to create whole melons. Melon harvests provide an average of five slices each while crafting a whole melon requires nine slices. This means that more melons must be planted than pumpkins. 
Planting nine melons for every five pumpkins will give a balanced production rate. The farm should therefore be built in multiple groups of fourteen (nine melons plus five pumpkins.) This tutorial builds a 28-plant farm which is two groups of fourteen. Therefore, eighteen melon plants and ten pumpkin plants are needed. 

Items Needed[]

Building the Farm[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Farm Layout 		 	 
See the image "Farm layout." The minimum area required is 21 x 12 blocks to contain the farm and machinery. The farm itself is 5 x 16. Dig a trench 14 blocks long. One bucket of water irrigates four blocks in each direction. So, place at least two buckets of water spaced to cover the 14-block length. Cover the trench with Slabs and place three torches spaced along the slabs.
Hoe out a 14-block strip on each side of the slabs and plant the melon and pumpkin seeds. At each end of the two plowed strips dig a hole and cover with a slab. This is to force the plants to place all of the melons and pumpkins in a straight line.

Rail Line[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Rail Line Layout 		 	 
See the image "Rail Line Layout" as a reference to directions used here. Place a Solid Block two blocks above the slab at the end of one of the planted strips. To the right of the block, dig a hole two blocks deep and place a Redstone Torch. Place a block of dirt over the redstone torch and then a Powered Rail on the dirt block. Add Rails parallel to the planted strips. When adjacent to the slab at the other end of the planted strip, place a powered rail and redstone torch. To the right of that, place a normal rail followed by an unpowered Powered Rail and a solid block. 

Harvesting Contraption[]
Place a Cart Assembler over the right most powered rail pointing along the track and set the rotation control to Lock Rotation. Place a Linear Chassis on top of the cart assembler with the light-colored sides facing along the track. Place five more linear chassis forming a line to the left of the first linear chassis. Place a chassis under the second and last chassis from the right. Set the sticky range of all of the linear chassis to 1 by holding Ctrl while using a Wrench on one of the linear chassis.
On the side of the contraption facing the farm, attach a Mechanical Drill to the ground-level linear chassis using a Slimeball. Attach a Chest or Barrel above the mechanical drill closest to the rail. Using a slimeball, attach a Portable Storage Interface to the linear chassis above the cart assembler. Use the wrench to face the portable storage interface away from the chest or barrel.
Place a mine cart in the cart assembler then power it by placing a redstone torch or Lever next to the cart assembler. Pick up the contraption using the wrench, then remove the cart assembler and power source. Replace the powered rail that popped off when removing the cart assembler. Finally, replace the contraption while standing behind the rail line's end block. (This assures that the contraption will face the right direction.)

Setting a Timer[]
Place a Redstone Repeater facing into the block behind contraption's cart and set the repeater to four ticks delay.  Place a Pulse Timer with its output touching the input of the redstone repeater. Set the delay to 5 minutes or as desired. Place a lever touching the input of the pulse timer. Turn the lever OFF to enable the timer. The triangle on the pulse timer will be dim. Turn the lever ON (triangle is bright red) to inhibit the timer.

Crafting Whole Melons[]
See the image "Crafter from Above" as a reference to directions used here. The crafter accepts pumpkins and melon slices from the contraption through the portable storage interface which places all the produce on a short belt. The belt runs through two brass tunnels which feed the melon slices through the crafter and divert the pumpkins to a bypass belt. The whole melons from the crafter are placed back on the bypass belt and fed into storage along with the pumpkins. The device is powered by a horizontal windmill.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Crafter from Above 		 	 
Building the Short Belt[]
Temporarily place a solid block on the ground next to the powered rail at the far end of the farm on the side away from the farm. Place two Shafts horizontal and end to end extending from the solid block away from the farm. Remove the solid block. Two spaces to the right of the far shaft, place another shaft in parallel. Place a Mechanical Belt between those two shafts. 

Building the Crafter[]
Build a 3 x 3 vertical array of Mechanical Crafters beginning immediately to the right of the mechanical belt. On the back side of the crafter, use the wrench to join all of the crafters together. On the front side, use the wrench to set the flow pattern to converge on the middle crafter of the right column and eject the product to the right. Place an Andesite Funnel on the left side of the crafter array so that the mechanical belt will feed items into the crafter.  Place a chest or barrel on the right side of the crafter array against the middle block to catch the output of the crafter array.

Building the Bypass Belt[]
Place a solid block on the ground immediately to the right of the output chest. Place a shaft extending horizontally from the solid block pointing toward the farm. Remove the solid block. Place a mechanical belt between the two available shafts. Place a chest or barrel with an andesite funnel at the right end of the bypass belt. Place another andesite funnel on the crafter's output chest so that the items empty on the belt. Use the wrench on the top of the andesite funnel to make the triangle on the top point to the belt. 

Installing the Item Handling Components[]
Place the two Brass Tunnels side by side on the two belts, one block to the right of the left end of the belts. Place a melon slice in the filter slot of the far side tunnel. Configure a List Filter to reject melon slices. Place the list filter in the filter slot of the nearside tunnel. Place a portable storage interface on the left side of the nearer tunnel then use the wrench to make it face toward the farm. On the back side of the portable storage interface, place an andesite funnel emptying on the end of the short belt. Use the wrench on the funnel to make the triangle on the top point toward the belt. 

Power Source[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Backside of the Melon Crafter Showing the Windmill 		 	 
See the image "Backside of the Melon Crafter Showing the Windmill" as a reference to directions used here. Place a Vertical Gearbox on the ground with one of the shafts attaching to the shaft of the short belt where it touches the crafter. Place two more vertical gearboxes on top of the first one using the same orientation. On the side of the top gearbox facing the belt, place a Cogwheel to power the crafter array.
Place a Rotational Speed Controller on the ground one block in front of the bottom gearbox. Turn the rotational speed controller so that the shaft does not connect to the gearbox. Place a Large Cogwheel in the rotational speed controller so that it connects with the middle gearbox.
Place a Windmill Bearing so that its shaft connects to the shaft of the rotational speed controller. Place a solid block on the sticky face of the windmill bearing. Attach 32 Windmill Sails to the solid block. Right click the windmill bearing to attach the sails and start the windmill. The direction on the windmill bearing does not matter. On the rotational speed controller, set the speed to 113 RPM and the direction to clockwise. 

Operating the Farm[]
The farm is now ready to operate. With the contraption placed on the unpowered powered rail, momentarily turn the lever on and back off. The contraption will launch and the timer will start. The farm will run continuously until the clock is interrupted by breaking any one of the redstone dust lines. The farm will produce an average of 24 melons and 24 pumpkins per hour. You will need to either empty the final chest regularly or feed it automatically into a larger storage system.

Usage[]
A Millstone can be powered by a Shaft from below or by a Cogwheel from the side.
There are two ways to insert items into a Millstone:

Dropping items on top of it: anything that can be processed will be picked up if the input buffer is empty.
Hoppers, Funnels, Chutes, and other inserters can directly feed it items from any side.
Once a valid item has been placed into the mill through any of the means listed above, the Millstone will begin to turn, and particles will appear around the machine. Once finished, the Millstone will not drop or output the result by itself, but there are two ways to remove processed items:

Right-clicking the Millstone with an empty hand: this will manually pick up everything in the output buffer.
Hoppers, Funnels, Chutes, and other exporters can pull items out of the output buffer from any side.
The Millstone takes time to process its inputs. The exact time depends on the Block Hardness and the amount of speed being fed into the machine. It follows the formula:

Minecart Coupling can be used to prevent Furnace Cart Contraptions from automatically taking the onboard fuel.

Saving, scanning, and printing Schematics has been implemented.
Videos[]

  	 	 			  



0.0.2[]
Create 0.0.2 is primarily a quality of life update to Create released on July 19th, 2019 for Minecraft version 1.14.

Changes[]

Gameplay[]
In-game items now have tooltip instructions.
Schematic placement tools now have complete descriptions.
Tweaks to Schematic And Quill.
Changed rendering order for blueprint overlay.

0.0.3[]
Create 0.0.3 is another update for Create primarily focusing on tweaking schematics which released on July 22nd, 2019 for Minecraft version 1.14. 
"The Schematicannon is still learning how to do its job."

Changes[]

Gameplay[]
Added Print option for schematics used in creative mode.

Fixes[]

Fixed server crash whenever Schematicannon ran out of materials.
Various fixes to the Schematicannon and schematics including:
Double blocks e.g. doors, beds, etc. being counted twice.
Beds not showing up in holograms.
Flowers being lost when schematics were scanned without soil.
Pistons not being placed correctly.

0.0.4[]
Create 0.0.4 is another update for Create released on July 28th, 2019 for Minecraft version 1.14. 
"This weeks addition: The Handheld Blockzapper!"

Additions[]

Items[]
 Handheld Blockzapper
A "combination of Building Wands and Block Exchangers".
Used for building and placing blocks at a distance.
Has 5 upgradable components.
Has an animated model.
 Blaze Brass[1]
 Chorus Chrome[1]

Changes[]

Items[]
Symmetry Wand received an animated model.
Some recipe unlock triggers have been changed.

Fixes[]

Fixed Schematicannon not using two items for double slabs.
Fixed Warn messages for client packets.
Trees no longer destroy Bedrock when boosted with Tree Fertilizer.
Fixed Symmetry Wand taking blocks from the inventory inconsistently.

0.0.5[]
Create 0.0.5 is another update for Create released on August 6th, 2019 for Minecraft version 1.14.

Technical[]

Support for forge version 28.0.45+

Upgrade Gear


Usage[]
When a Netherite Diving Helmet is worn with a full Netherite Backtank, Netherite Leggings, and either Netherite Diving Boots or Netherite Boots, the wearer is immune to Fire and Lava. Immunity is lost when the Backtank runs out of Air Pressure. Like Netherite, the Netherite Diving Gear will not burn when thrown into Fire or Lava.
Unlike Copper Diving Boots, it is still possible to ascend in Lava while wearing Netherite Diving Boots if the jump key is held for longer.

Armor[]
When worn, the Helmet provides 3 () Armor points, the Netherite Backtank provides 8 () Armor points, and the Diving Boots provide 3 () Armor points.

Air Pressure[]
Main article: Copper Backtank
Like the Copper Backtank, the Netherite Backtank stores Air Pressure. It can be filled by being placed as a block and powered with Rotational Force from the Shaft at the top. The Air Pressure can also be used for tools like the Potato Cannon.

In-Game Tooltips[]
Netherite Diving Helmet[]
Together with a Netherite Backtank, this will protect you from extreme heat. To be effective, Legs and Feet have to be covered in Netherite, too.
When Worn (Full set)
Provides immunity to Fire and Lava, slowly draining Air Pressure from the Backtank. Also grants improved vision in Lava.

Netherite Backtank[]
A Wearable Tank for carrying Pressurized Air.
When Worn
Provides Pressurized Air to equipment that requires it.
When placed, Powered by Kinetics
Collects Pressurized Air at a rate dependent on Rotational Speed.

Netherite Diving Boots[]
A pair of heavy boots, allowing for better traversal of the Ocean floor, including Oceans made of Lava.
When Worn
Wielder descends more quickly in liquids. Grants the ability to walk and jump underwater. Wielder also is no longer affected by Mechanical Belts.

Gallery[]
Under Lava vision improved by the Netherite Diving Gear. The underside of Lava falls and Striders can be seen.

Usage[]
Displaying Redstone signal strength[]
A Nixie Tube may be used to display Redstone signal strength of the connected redstone component. It will display the highest connected signal strength.

Displaying Characters[]
When right clicked with a named Name Tag or a Clipboard with text, the Nixie Tube as well as adjacent Nixie Tubes will display the text.

Colors[]
When right clicked with a Dye the color of the text can be changed. The Dye is not consumed.

Display Link[]
Nixie Tubes can serve as a source and target for Display Links. When used as a source, the content of the Nixie Tubes can be copied to a target.

Train Signal[]
Main article: Train Signal
Nixie Tubes can be placed on Train Signals to give railway signals.

Trivia[]
Nixie Tubes exist in real life (see Wikipedia)

Nozzle
Andesite Alloy +  Any Wool



Usage[]
A Nozzle can only be placed on the face of an Encased Fan. It redirects the effects of the fan in every direction except directly behind it, pushing or pulling entities toward or away from the nozzle in a range one block shorter than the range of the fan itself. 
The effects of nozzles stack with others nearby. A cluster of nozzles at maximum RPM can easily send the player hundreds of blocks in any direction.
Players that are Sneaking or flying in creative mode are unaffected by the nozzle.

title: Overview
summary: Create is a Minecraft modification that reimagines automation through the use of Rotational Force, supplementing traditional redstone systems with a visually intuitive mechanical power network. Players generate and transmit kinetic energy to drive machines that move items, process materials, and con...
content:
Create is a Minecraft modification that reimagines automation through the use of Rotational Force, supplementing traditional redstone systems with a visually intuitive mechanical power network. Players generate and transmit kinetic energy to drive machines that move items, process materials, and construct dynamic contraptions. The mod also introduces fluid handling, enabling the transport and transformation of liquids using animated pumps, pipes, and spouts. A standout feature is its realistic train system, which allows players to build steam-powered locomotives, schedule routes, and transport goods or passengers across vast distances. To support learning and experimentation, Create integrates with the Just Enough Items (JEI) mod, providing in-game access to crafting recipes, machine usage, and sequenced assembly steps.


Item Processing & Automation[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Create offers a multi-step, immersive approach to automation that goes beyond simple crafting:

Crushing Wheels: Break down ores and blocks into finer materials.
Mechanical Press: Compact items or shape metal sheets.
Mixers & Basins: Combine ingredients into alloys, dough, or potions.
Deployers: Simulate right-click actions for crafting or block interaction.
Sequenced Assembly: Automate complex crafting recipes with precision timing.
Fluid Processing: Fluids such as water, lava, and potions can be pumped, mixed, and dispensed using spouts, hoses, and smart pipes.
JEI integration allows players to view recipes and machine interactions directly in-game, making it easier to understand and replicate complex setups.

Moving Contraptions[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Create enables dynamic, mobile machines that can rotate or travel through the world:

Mechanical Bearings: Rotate entire structures like windmills or turntables.
Piston Contraptions: Extend and retract block assemblies.
Minecart & Train Contraptions: Build automated trains with customizable carriages, stations, and steam-powered engines. Trains can carry items, passengers, or entire contraptions across long distances.
Gantries & Pulleys: Move contraptions and structures vertically to create things like elevators and mineshaft drills,
Train systems are fully integrated with Create’s automation tools, allowing for scheduled deliveries, loading/unloading stations, and immersive transport networks.

Logistics & Transport[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Efficient item and fluid transport is a hallmark of the mod:

Belt Networks & Chain Conveyors: Visually satisfying conveyors move items between machines.
Funnels & Chutes: Control item input/output with filters and timing.
Smart Pipes & Pumps: Transport fluids with mechanical precision, including vertical pumping and directional flow.
Redstone Link: Wireless redstone communication for remote control.
Train Cargo: Items and fluids can be loaded into train carriages and routed across stations using schedules and filters.
Return to Tutorials

Crafting[]

Package Frogport
Slimeball +  Item Vault +  Andesite Alloy



Usage[]
Placement[]
Right-click the chain of a Chain Conveyor to set the frogport’s target, then place the frogport. Frogports can be placed up to 4 blocks to the side and down from their target chain.

Address[]
The frogport will only take packages that match its address. The address can be set by right-clicking the placed frogport or in it's UI. Frogport names also support custom simplified RegEx syntax (check Cardboard Package: RegEx).
The frogport will only send packages that don’t match its address unless its set to “only send packages” in its UI.

Inventory[]
The Frogport has 18 slots of inventory. It automatically takes from and deposits to inventories below it. It puts unmatching Cardboard Packages on the Chain Conveyor, and deposits matching packages to the inventory below it.

Usage[]
Packing[]
Main article: Cardboard Package
When placed adjacent to any inventory, Packagers can create Cardboard Packages from the inventory they’re attached to. The process does not require extra materials.
When powered with a redstone signal, the packager attempts to fill the package as much as possible. A Cardboard Package has 9 slots of inventory. Placing a written sign on the Packager labels the created Cardboard Package with an address to be sent to.
When a Stock Link is placed on a Packager, the Packager can receive requests from a Logistics Network. It can create packages with an address, specific items, and a specific amount of items.

Usage[]
Creating a Haunted Bell[]
Placing a Peculiar Bell above a Soul Fire or Haunting it will create a Haunted Bell.

On Contraptions[]
The Peculiar Bell, as well as the Haunted Bell and village Bell, will toll every time a contraption stops, starts, or changes directions. When placed in the center of a Mechanical Bearing contraption, the bell will toll for every full rotation. When placed in the center of a Minecart Contraption, the bell will toll every time the minecart begins to move. When placed to the right or left of a Minecart Contraption, the bell will toll for right and left turns, respectively.

Usage[]
The Placard is primarily used to display items for decoration. It emits a short Redstone pulse, the same length as a stone button, when right clicked with the same item it is holding. Unlike Item Frames, it will stick to Contraptions, and items cannot be rotated once placed inside. The Placard also does not interact with the Comparator; there will be no redstone output regardless of whether or not an item is inside the placard.

content:
Polished Rose Quartz


	
		
		
	
	



	
	



	
		Renewable
	
	Yes

	Yes (64)



Polished Rose Quartz is an important crafting material used in the production of Electron Tubes. It can also be used to craft Rose Quartz Lamps, or its tiled decorative blocks.

Contents

1 Obtaining
2 Usage

2.1 Crafting Ingredient
2.2 Block Cutting


3 Data values

3.1 ID


4 History
5 Trivia



Obtaining[]
Polished Rose Quartz is created through Polishing, which can be done manually by holding Rose Quartz and Sand Paper in both the main and offhand, and using the Sandpaper. It can also be created when the Rose Quartz is in item form, by using the Sandpaper after the Rose Quartz is thrown out of the Inventory.
As with all Manual Item Application recipes, Polished Rose Quartz production can be automated through the use of Deployers.

content:
Pondering is an in-game guide system that allows the player to quickly get information about Create blocks.
The pondering screen shows an example contraption that explains the functions of the block.

 	https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Windmill_Bearing_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scene for a Windmill Bearing. 		 	 
Contents

1 Usage

1.1 Keybinds
1.2 Navigation
1.3 Ponder Categories


2 History



Usage[]
The full Ponder Index can be accessed through the Create menu by clicking the  Engineer's Goggles icon in the pause menu.
An item can be Pondered by hovering over it in the inventory and holding forward ("W" by default) until the bar below the item is filled up. This displays an animated infographic about the item being pondered. 

Keybinds[]
The keybinds for ponder are the same as those for certain player actions.

Q - Activate Identify mode. This pauses the current ponder scene. Hovering over Create elements shows the name of the block and gives the option to ponder those elements.
S - Restart the current animation.
A or D - Go backwards or forwards a scene, if available.
E - Close the animation.
Comfy Reading does not currently have a keybind, but can be enabled by tapping the button in the bottom right. This slows down the entire animation to help read the text boxes. 

Navigation[]
While Pondering, similar or relevant machines can be viewed by clicking the icon to the left or activating identify mode and holding W over a visible component. After moving away from the initially pondered item, the option to "Think Back" can be found at the bottom left. The player can skip to specific parts of an animation by clicking different sections of the gray bar at the bottom.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scene for a Water Wheel. 		 	 
Ponder Categories[]
The categories ponders are sorted into in-game.

  Kinetic Blocks - Components which help relaying Rotational Force elsewhere
  Kinetic Sources - Components which generate Rotational Force
  Kinetic Appliances - Components which make use of Rotational Force
 Fluid Manipulators - Components which help relaying and making use of Fluids
 Item Transportation - Components which help moving items around
 Logic Components - Components which help with Redstone Engineering
 Creative Mode - Components not usually available in Survival Mode
 Movement Anchors - Components which allow the creation of moving Contraptions, animating an attached structure in a variety of ways.
 Contraption Actors - Components which expose special behavior when attached to a Contraption.
 Block Attachment Utility - Tools and Components used to assemble structures moved as an animated Contraption.
 Railway Equipment - Components used in the construction or management of Train contraptions
Recent Changes - Components that have been added or changed significantly in recent versions of create
History[]
0.5.1: Added a ponder category for recently added/changed blocks

The Portable Fluid Interface is the fluid version of the Portable Storage Interface. It is used to insert or extract from the fluid inventory of a Contraption.

Contents

Obtaining[]

Recipe




Portable Fluid Interface
Copper Casing +  Chute



Usage[]
The Interfaces must be placed facing each other at 1-2 blocks apart, one on a Contraption with Fluid Tanks and one stationary. A Fluid Pump is required to insert or extract liquid from the Contraption. To pump liquids to another tank, simply connect the stationary interface and the fluid tank with fluid pipes, although pumps are required to move the liquids.
Contraptions will automatically stall for an Interface. A Redstone signal can be applied to break off the connection early.

The Portable Storage Interface is a block that allows Item Transporters to directly interact with Contraption inventories.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Crafting
1.2 Wrench


2 Usage

2.1 Transferring Items


3 Data values

3.1 ID


4 History



Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Portable Storage Interface

Andesite Casing +  Chute





Wrench[]
Shift-right-clicking on a Portable Storage Interface with a Wrench will destroy the Portable Storage Interface and place it in your inventory.

Usage[]
Transferring Items[]
 	https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Portable_Storage_Interface_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scene for the Portable Storage Interface. 		 	 
Portable Storage Interfaces are used on Contraptions.
For Portable Storage Interfaces to interact they must face each other at 1 to 2 blocks apart. One interface must be on a Contraption, while the other is stationary.
The Contraption must have an inventory such as a Chest or Barrel, while the stationary interface has something inserting or extracting directly from it, such as a Funnel, Chute, or Hopper. Inventory will then be exchanged at the rate of the inserting or extracting component.
Contraptions will stall when interfaces meet. A Redstone signal can be applied to break off the connection.
The connection automatically breaks off when no transfer has been done for a certain number of ticks. The default is 60 ticks, but the exact timeout is configurable via the psiTimeout setting. If the stationary side is not extracting items quickly enough (e.g. a funnel onto a slow belt), the connection may break off before the transfer is complete. To prevent this issue, extract the items from the stationary interface with a fast Chute directly into an inventory as a buffer, then use a Funnel to extract from that buffer onto the belt.

Usage[]
Appearance[]
The Postbox can come in 16 different colors. It has a red flag much like the Train Station that is automatically raised when the Postbox has anything in its inventory.

Trains[]
Right-click a Train Station with a Postbox to link it to that station. The Postbox can be placed up to 4 blocks away from the station. Set its Address in its UI. 
The Postbox will move Cardboard Packages to and from Trains with an inventory that stop at its linked Train Station. It will take packages with a matching address or deposit packages that don’t match its address.
When used with item transporting blocks such as a Chute or Funnel, the Postbox only allows packages matching its Address to be extracted from it.
It can also be set to only send packages in its UI.
Mailbox names also support custom simplified RegEx syntax (check Cardboard Package: RegEx).

Obtaining[]
Mechanical Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Potato Cannon
Andesite Alloy +Precision Mechanism +Fluid Pipe +Copper Ingot
7


Usage[]
When fired while wearing a Copper or Netherite Backtank, no durability is used, rather, 4.5 seconds of air is consumed. If the Potato Cannon is fired while either not wearing a Backtank or wearing an empty Backtank, the cannon's durability is consumed instead.
When a Potato Cannon is held in both hands, the firing cooldown for both cannons is multiplied by 
  
    
      
        
          2
          3
        
      
    
    {\displaystyle \frac{2}{3}}
  
, resulting in a fire rate 50% faster than usual. The cannons alternate firing, rather than firing simultaneously. Ammunition with cooldowns below 15 ticks fire faster than the damage cooldown on entities, resulting in many shots phasing through the target.
A Potato Cannon can be enchanted with Looting, Punch, Power, Unbreaking, Curse of Vanishing, Mending, Flame, and Potato Recovery.

Potato Recovery gives all ammo a chance to drop as an item on hit. The chance of ammo being dropped is 25% for Potato Recovery 1, 33% for Potato Recovery 2, and 50% for Potato Recovery 3.
Power increases the damage a projectile will deal +20% damage per level.
Flame causes the target to take 1 damage every 10 ticks, for 40 ticks (2 seconds). This overrides the fire inflicted by the Baked Potato. Flame does not deal extra damage with Poisonous Potatoes, unless the attacked entity is immune to poison.
Blocks cannot be mined with a Potato Cannon held in the main hand.

title: Precision Workshop
summary: The precision workshop gives you the tools to build just about anything in the Create mod. In addition to the bulk mixing provided by the Brass Workshop, the precision workshop enables you to build Precision Mechanisms, Crushing Wheels, and Train Tracks. Precision mechanisms allow you to build Rotat...
content:
The precision workshop gives you the tools to build just about anything in the Create mod. In addition to the bulk mixing provided by the Brass Workshop, the precision workshop enables you to build Precision Mechanisms, Crushing Wheels, and Train Tracks. Precision mechanisms allow you to build Rotation Speed Controllers, Train Controls, and other advanced devices. Crushing wheels open up a world of automated ore processing for Iron Farms, Nuggets of Experience and more. This design does not include bulk washing or vanilla automation such as bulk smelting.


Precision Workshop
Precision Workshop
Contents

1 Production Centers

1.1 Bulk Mixer with Press
1.2 Precision Mechanism Line
1.3 Train Track Line
1.4 Mechanical Crafter Assembly


2 Power System

2.1 Stress and Speed Requirements
2.2 Method of Power Production
2.3 Converting Rotational Speed
2.4 Power Distribution





Production Centers[]
The precision workshop has four production centers which are described below. 

Bulk Mixer with Press[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Bulk Mixer with Press 		 	 
This is a very compact combination of a high speed Mechanical Press and a Mechanical Mixer set up for heated bulk processing. The image "Bulk Mixer with Press" shows the layout. Rotational power enters from the shaft on the left connecting to the press which is two blocks above a Depot. The press passes rotational power on to a vertical gear box which turns a cogwheel driving the mixer. The mixer is placed two blocks above a Basin The basin is heated by a Blaze Burner below it, fed by a hopper on the left, and outputs to a Mechanical Belt on the right. The mechanical belt is powered from the mixer through the cogwheel on the right which feeds into a vertical gearbox that changes the axis of rotation to horizontal. A vertical belt conveys the rotation to the horizontal belt which conveys the mixer output through an Andesite Funnel into a barrel.
To operate the press, simply place an item or a stack of items on the depot. Pick up the items when the pressing is complete. For the bulk mixer, place the ingredients into the hopper on the left in the proper proportions. Feed the blaze burner a fuel item if needed. Collect the processed items from the barrel. 

Precision Mechanism Line[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Precision Mechanism Manufacturing Line 		 	 
This is a basic manufacturing line for low-rate production of precision mechanisms. A fully automated production line can be found on the Tutorials/Crafting Precision Mechanisms page. The image "Precision Mechanism Manufacturing Line" depicts the design used in this workshop. Three Deployers are placed two blocks above a mechanical belt. Rotational power enters from the shaft on the left and is passed from one deployer to another. The first deployer has a cogwheel filter. The second has a large cogwheel filter. And the third has iron nugget. The process requires a lot of cogwheels and nuggets. The hoppers and barrels above the deployers allow you to stock a large number of components.
The manufacturing process begins by placing Golden Sheets in the barrel on the left. They are released one at a time to the conveyer belt. After the deployers add their components, the partially complete precision mechanisms are stored in the barrel on the right. You must then move the partially complete mechanisms to the left side barrel for the next round of components. The golden sheets and partially complete precision mechanisms must be run through the manufacturing line a total of five times before they are complete.

Train Track Line[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Train Track Manufacturing Line 		 	 
This manufacturing line is quite similar in design to the precision mechanism line described above except the right most deployer is replace with a mechanical press and both deployers are filtered with iron ingots. Unlike precision mechanisms, however, train tracks do not require multiple passes through the line. You can fill the input barrel with stone slabs and the deployer barrels with ingots then let the line run autonomously for true bulk production of tracks.

Mechanical Crafter Assembly[]
This workshop is designed to power the 21 mechanical crafters required to build a crushing wheel. You may, however, reconfigure the mechanical crafters for any other recipe with confidence that there will be sufficient power. 

Power System[]
There are four factors which must be addressed when designing a power system: 1) stress and speed requirements, 2) method of power production, 3) converting rotational speed, and 4) power distribution. I will step through each of these.

Stress and Speed Requirements[]
This design has several devices with high stress-unit needs. The table titled "Stress Unit Requirements" lists all of the power consuming devices along with the stress units they consume at one RPM (SU/RPM). Multiplying the SU/RPM by the number of each type of device and summing the subtotals shows that the total consumption is 82 SU/RPM.  


Stress Unit Requirements


Devices

SU/RPM

# Devices

Subtotal SU/RPM


Mechanical Press

8

2

16


Mechanical Mixer

4

1

4


Deployer

4

5

20


Mechanical Crafter

2

21

42


Total SU/RPM Required

82

The next step is to decide what speed (RPM) you want the system to run at. Each device could be powered at a different RPM, but for simplicity, this design is based on 64 RPM. Multiplying 64 RPM x 82 SU/RPM gives a total of 5248 SU. We must now design a power supply that gives us at least that amount.

Method of Power Production[]
The first step is to decide upon Water Wheels, a Windmill, or a Steam Engine. 

A water wheel produces 256 SU. A large water wheel produces 512 SU. Dividing the total power requirement of 5248 SU by 256 and 512 respectively gives a need for 21 water wheels or 11 large water wheels. That many water wheels would be an inelegant design.
A single windmill can provide up to 8192 SU depending on the number of sails used. So, a single windmill would be suitable for this workshop.
A single steam engine can provide up to 16,384 SU which is more than enough. But it is much more complex to build than a windmill.
A single windmill will, therefore, be the power producer for this workshop. The next step is to determine how many sails are need. A chart on the Windmill page shows the power produced for a given number of sails. You can calculate this directly, however, by noting that each group of eight sails adds 512 SU to the windmill's power output. Note that groups of less than eight add nothing. So, 8 to 15 sails produce 512 SUs, 16 to 23 produce 1024 and so on. If we divide our total requirement of 5248 SU by 512, we get that we need 10.25 groups of eight sails. Rounding that up to 11 gives us a need for 88 sails.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Windmill Power System 		 	 
Converting Rotational Speed[]
Windmills do not run at constant speed like water wheels do. Each group of eight sails adds one to the RPM. So, 11 groups (88 sails) outputs 11 RPM. We need to convert that to 64 RPM. A Rotation Speed Controller can do that very easily. But building a rotation speed controller requires a precision mechanism, which we won't have until we build this workshop. So, we will use Adjustable Chain Gearshift instead.
Each pair of fully-powered adjustable-chain gearshifts doubles the rotation speed. One set will double 11 RPM to 22. A second set will give 44 RPM. And a third would give 88 RPM which is more the 64 that we designed for. To get 64 instead of 88, we will power the third set of adjustable chain gearshifts with an Analog Lever rather than the standard lever used on the first two sets. An analog lever outputs an adjustable redstone signal strength which can vary the multiplication factor of the adjustable chain gearshift between 1.0 and 2.0. A signal strength of six on the adjustable chain gearshift gives a final rotation speed of 63.5 RPM...close enough.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Full Precision Workshop 		 	 
Power Distribution[]
Getting the power from the generator to each of the components at the right height and axis of rotation is one of the most complex aspects of design. Running shafts and belts along with changing axes and directions of rotation can add a complex exoskeleton to your system. Many otherwise elegant designs become very messy when consideration of power distribution is left to the end. 
It is best to think of power distribution in the early design of the system. Build your components first, the power distribution system second, and the power generator last. That will give you the most convenient location for the generator and avoid complex twists and turns in the power distribution.
Try to get the rotation inputs to all of your components aligned at the same height and direction. This makes the power distribution simple and efficient as can be seen with the single master drive belt at the back in the image "Full Precision Workshop."  Keep the power transmission devices (shafts, belts, gears, etc.) out of the way so they don't impede your movement. It is often easiest to run power for mechanisms overhead and power for conveyor belts underground. The image "Full Precision Workshop" shows that I kept the power distribution for the belts and mechanical crafters above ground. This was to make them easier for you to see. But I kept them at the back of the system so they would rarely be tripped over. The belt for the mixer is further forward than the others. Rather than putting a shaft across the front end of the workshop, which would get in the way, I chose to run a belt down from the mixer power. You can also add andesite or brass casings to the shafts either for aesthetics or ease of walking over them.

Crafting[]


Name

Recipe




Pulse Timer

Amethyst Shard +  Brass Sheet +  Redstone Torch +  Any Stone





Usage[]
The Pulse Timer sends a redstone signal repeatedly with a set amount of time between each pulse. It can be disabled by powering it with a redstone signal. 
The interval can be set in its Value Settings Screen accessed by holding right-click. The delay can be set between 2 ticks and 60 minutes. The settings can also be copied and pasted to other Pulse Timers, Pulse Repeaters, or Pulse Extenders by using a Clipboard.
The Pulse Timer can be inverted by right-clicking it. This causes it to be on by default, instead turning off for 2 ticks every interval. Powering it in this state keeps it on.

content:
Task

Purpose

Steps



1. Make Andesite Alloy


Andesite Alloy is a fundamental ingredient for nearly every item in Create. You will need a lot of it.


1. Mine iron ore and andesite blocks
2. Use JEI to find the recipe for Andesite Alloy
3. Make a full stack




2. Ride a spinning turntable


Rotational power is needed to run machines. Learn to generate power and control its speed and stress capacity.


1. Make a stack of Shafts. Use JEI for the recipe.
2. Make a half stack of Cogwheels.
3. Make a half dozen Large Cogwheels.
4. Make two Gearboxes. Consult the Build Order page and trace the dependencies for a gear box.
5. Make and install a Water Wheel.
6. Explore the use of shafts, cogwheels, and gearboxes to increase/decrease rotation speed and change the direction of rotation.
7. Build a Turntable. Place it on a rotating vertical shaft, then stand on it.




3. Make a Slimeball


Learn the use of a mill and some of the recipes it provides.


1. Build a Millstone and connect it to your rotational power source. Run it at the fastest speed you can.
2. Create Dough by milling wheat into flour and combining with a bucket of water on a crafting table.
3. Combine dough with Lime Dye on a crafting table.




4. Cut down a tree with a Mechanical Saw


Build your first Create contraption! Build your starter workshop, learn about mechanical pistons, mechanical presses and gearshifts. See how the mechanical saw cuts down the whole tree at once.


1. Build a Starter Workshop
2. Build eight Piston Extension Poles 
3. Build a Mechanical Piston
4. Create 3 Iron Sheets on a Mechanical Press
5. Build a Mechanical Saw
6. Build a Gearshift
7. Place the mechanical piston on the ground horizontally with two extra extension poles.
8. Attach the gearshift to the mechanical piston and to a rotational power source.
9. Attach a Lever to the gearshift. This will allow you to move the piston in and out.
10. Coat the piston with slime from a slime ball, then attach the mechanical saw.
11. Activate the lever until the piston fully retracts.
12. Plant a tree two blocks in front of the saw.
13. When the tree matures, activate the lever to push the saw into the tree.




5. Mine some ore with a contraption


Create a minecart contraption. Learn about mechanical drills, cart assemblers, placement assist and the various issues influencing the design of mining contraptions.


1. Build a dozen Mechanical Drills
2. Build 15 Linear Chassis
3. Build a Cart Assembler
4. Build a Wrench
5. Build a minecart, rail, and powered rail.
6. Build 2 chests.
7. Review Tutorials/Mining Contraptions and build a simple 3 x 4 mining contraption with manual rails and no portable storage interface. Use Placement Assist to keep the drills aligned.
8. Use the cart assembler to assemble the contraption and use the wrench to pick up the assembled contraption.
9. Lay rail along a tunnel in rock. Place the contraption on powered rail and give it a push to start.



6. Automatically Plant & Harvest Trees.

Learn to create brass, create electron tubes and smart chutes, build deployers, and automate log production


1. Create a half stack of Electron Tubes
2. Build a Brass Workshop
3. Create a stack of Brass Ingots
4. Create 9 Deployers
5. Create one Smart Chute
6. Follow the instructions in Tutorials/Tree Automation to build and run your tree farm.



7. Build an iron farm.

Learn how to build mechanical crafters, mechanical belts, encased fans and crushing wheels. Learn how to automate large scale ore processing.


1. Create a stack of Brass Ingots
2. Build 21 Mechanical Crafters
3. Create 2 Crushing Wheels
4. Build 5 Encased Fans
5. Build a dozen Mechanical Belts
6. Review the example in Tutorials/Iron Ingot Automation then design and build your own iron ore processor.



8. Build a Train.

Learn how to create precision mechanisms, sturdy sheets, and eight types of train components.


1. Build a Precision Workshop.
2. Build a Precision Mechanism
3. Review the Train page and links for how to build a train.
4. Design and build your own train and rail system.



9. Build a Logistics Network.

Find your own way through the extremely powerful and complex High Logistics upgrade. Build mass storage systems, automated item retrievals, and fully automate resource management for factories.


1. Review the information and links in Logistics Network
2. Design and build your own concept.


Feedback[]
Feedback really helps with projects like this. So please leave a comment below when you complete any of the tasks above and give some feedback on anything that can be improved.

Usage[]
Connecting Structures[]
Unlike Linear Chassis, the Radial Chassis connects to a radius of blocks around it rather than a straight line of blocks. This can be unwieldy if there are blocks nearby one would rather not connect to the Contraption.
You can right click on the sides of the chassis while holding a Slimeball or Super Glue to make them sticky, and again to apply it to all sides. The items are not consumed. The radius of affected blocks can be changed per chassis with a Wrench. Hold Ctrl to scroll every connected chassis.

content:
Introduction[]
Randomizer is mechanism that dispenses different levels of signal randomly. Even though various variants of redstone randomizers existed, most of them had defects with compactness and regulation. Using Create modification, these defects can be fixed and modified as player wishes. So this page will help you construct your randomizer using simple components.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			This is how working 3-output randomizer must look like. Golden blocks mean outputs of random signals. 		 	 
Process of constructing is divided by steps for comfortable reading. Screenshots are provided.
Also should be noted that this is 3-output randomizer, which can be modernized up to 4-output one.



Construction[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 1 		 	 
Step 1:  Create a small platform 5x5 or 7x7 scale. Also you need 4 blocks high free space.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 2 		 	 


Step 2: Put three blocks, put dropper on top and hopper forward it. Note: hopper must be set straight down.



 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 3 		 	 

Step 3: Connect brass funnels to dropper and vanilla hopper. Take attention to the arrows on them: funnel with dropper must be set as taking in, funnel with vanila hopper must be set as extracting.


 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 4 		 	 

Step 4:  Connect vanilla hoppers to chutes that lead to dropper as shown in screenshot. The same must be done on the other side.



 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 5 		 	 
Step 5:  Place encased fan facing into the chute and place underneath creative motor (if in Creative mode) or any other regulable source of rotational force for it to push items into the funnel. The same must be done on the other side.



 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 6 		 	 

Step 6: This step requires two different 64(16)-stackable items and one non-stackable item. Here we will use wool, wooden axe and snowball. Put snowball into the brass funnel filters on the side and change droppable items number into 1, using mousewheel.
Take filter (andesite or brass one) and add wooden axe and wool into white-list. Put them on the other side of randomizer and also put droppable items number as 1.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 7: setting the filter 		 	 
Step 7:  Since the main part is done, we have to make it into random signals. Put redstone comparators in front of vanilla hoppers; put block just forward the comparator that will detect wool and wooden axe. The snowball one can generate signal all by itself and we`re not going to touch it.


 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 7: filters are already put 		 	 





 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Step 8 		 	 
Step 8:  Make redstone contraption as shown on screenshot.
And... we`ve finished! The only thing you have to do now is to put wool, axe and snowball into the dropper and check the working. If something is wrong, please re-check your randomizer on mistakes. 
P.S. If you need unequal chances of signal outputs (for example, 50%-25%-25%), you have to add more items to create same ratio (for example, if you need 50%-25%-25%, you can put two wool, one axe and one snowball).
Enjoy your randomizer!

Modernization[]
 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			4-output randomizer 		 	 
Of course, this machine can be modernized up to 4-output randomizer. 
Modernization of 4-output is actually a repeating of 7-8 steps, just on the second side, but we also take into filter golden hoe (or any other non-stackable item) along with snowball as non-stackable item and 16(64)-stacked item. The result must look like on the screenshot at the right. Most importantly, don`t forget to put golden hoe into the dropper for it to work properly.
P.S. If you don`t like the output locations and you want to change it, you can use wireless redstone link to navigate the signal in 128 blocks range.

Usage[]
Merging Packages from a request[]
Whenever a logistical request for a Mechanical Crafter is sent from multiple points, the delay between the packages often breaks the recipe. This is solved by the Re-Packager. All incoming packages can be collected in an adjacent inventory, and whenever one order has fully arrived, the Re-Packager takes them and merges them into a single package, which can then be sent to the Crafter.

Create adds several components that can be used in Redstone Circuits. These include the Redstone Contact, Redstone Link, Linked Controller, Pulse Repeater, Pulse Extender, Pulse Timer, Powered Latch, and Powered Toggle Latch. These components can make redstone circuits simpler and smaller as well as giving finer control over timing.

Contents

1 Obtaining

1.1 Crafting


2 Usage

2.1 Redstone Link
2.2 Analog Lever
2.3 Pulse Extender

2.3.1 Pulse Length
2.3.2 Circuit Behaviors


2.4 Pulse Repeater

2.4.2 Circuit Behaviors


2.5 Pulse Timer
2.6 Powered Latch

2.6.1 Continuous Signals
2.6.2 Manual Operation

2.7 Powered Toggle Latch

Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Redstone Link

Transmitter +  Andesite Casing
2



Analog Lever

Stick +  Andesite Casing





Pulse Extender

Redstone +  Brass Sheet +  Redstone Torch +  Any Stone





Pulse Repeater

Redstone Dust +  Brass Sheet +  Redstone Torch +  Any Stone





Pulse Timer

Amethyst Shard +  Brass Sheet +  Redstone Torch +  Any Stone





Powered Latch

Redstone Torch +  Redstone Dust +  Lever +  Any Stone





Powered Toggle Latch

Redstone Torch +  Lever +  Any Stone





Usage[]
Redstone Link[]
Redstone links transfer redstone signals across long distances, keeping their redstone signal strength. Receivers will output the strongest redstone strength received from sending links.
To toggle the redstone link between sending and receiving a signal, hold Shift and right click it or right click with a Wrench.  A redstone link in receiving mode will show a signal dish on the antenna.  Assign an item or block to at least one of the two frequency slots, and the redstone link will only send or receive signals to or from links with matching frequency slots.
The redstone link has a signal strength of a radius of 256 blocks, which does not require line-of-sight and thus can be placed underground, in a separate structure, etc.  Note that the redstone link seems to have a 'default state' of OFF, and any redstone links that are actively receiving when a world is saved will briefly pulse OFF when the world is loaded again; this can cause unintended behaviors in contraptions that rely upon heavily active links.
Redstone links can be remotely controlled using the Linked Controller added in Create 0.3.2.


Analog Lever[]
Emits a redstone signal with an adjustable strength. Right click to make it higher, shift right click to make it lower. The current signal strength can be viewed by looking at the lever while wearing Engineer's Goggles.


 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Extender 		 	 
Pulse Extender[]
A pulse extender extends pulses. It emits a variable length pulse immediately after receiving a trigger signal. The output is normally off by default  and emits a powered pulse when triggered. 
It can also be inverted to be normally on and emit a negative (power off) pulse by right-clicking it. Regardless of which mode it is in, the device will begin outputting a pulse immediately after detecting the ascending edge (off to on) of a redstone signal. The pulse will remain on as long as the trigger signal is on. The pulse length timer begins counting down only after the device detects a descending edge (on to off) of the trigger signal. Once the device is triggered, additional signal pulses will be ignored until the active pulse is complete.

Pulse Length[]
The pulse length can be changed by placing the crosshairs over the center of the device and moving the scroll wheel on the mouse. Pulse lengths can be set from 2-19 ticks, 1-59 seconds, and 1-30 minutes. The device will accept changes to the pulse length after the ascending edge trigger and before the descending edge trigger.  After the descending edge trigger, the device will accept changes that shorten the pulse length but ignore changes that lengthen it.

Circuit Behaviors[]
Similar to a redstone repeater, a pulse extender acts as a diode transmitting a signal only in one direction. It outputs a signal strength of 15 regardless of the input strength thus behaving as a circuit extender. And it can both power and draw power from opaque blocks.


 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Repeater 		 	 
Pulse Repeater[]
A pulse repeater is a redstone device that emits a pulse a set delay after receiving a trigger signal. It can also be set to output a redstone signal by default and to emit a negative pulse after the time delay. Right-clicking the device toggles it between positive and negative pulse outputs. Regardless of the type of pulse selected, the device is triggered on the ascending edge of a redstone signal (off to on). Additional trigger signals will be ignored until after the pulse is complete. 

Delay Settings[]
The delay can be changed by placing the crosshairs over the center of the device and moving the scroll wheel on the mouse. Delay times can be set from 2-19 ticks, 1-59 seconds, and 1-30 minutes. Once the device is triggered and the delay is counting down, changes to the delay time will not take effect until the currently triggered pulse is done.

Circuit Behaviors[]
Similar to a redstone repeater, a pulse repeater acts as a diode transmitting a signal only in one direction. It outputs a signal strength of 15 regardless of the input strength thus behaving as a circuit extender. And it can both power and draw power from opaque blocks.


 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Pulse Timer 		 	 
Pulse Timer[]
A pulse timer acts like a clock circuit, repeatedly outputting a pulse with a manually-set time between pulses. The pulse timing can be between 2 tick and 60 minutes. Pulse timers can be inverted by right-clicking, causing it to be on by default with short off pulses.





 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Powered Latch 		 	 
Powered Latch[]
A powered latch has two inputs (a set and reset) and one output. The side with the redstone torch is the output. The opposite side is the set line. Either of the other two sides can act as the reset line. A pulse to the set line will power the latch which will maintain a powered output until a pulse is detected on the reset line.  When the output is on, any pulses to the set line will be ignored. When the output is off, any pulses to the reset line will be ignored. Both the set and reset actions are triggered on the ascending edge of the pulse.

Continuous Signals[]
When continuous signals are applied rather than pulses, the behavior of the powered latch becomes more complicated. If the output is off when power is applied to the set line, the output will turn on regardless of the state of the reset signal. If the set line is subsequently turned off, then the output will remain on if the reset line is unpowered but will turn off if the reset line is powered.  If the output is on when power is applied to the reset line, the output will turn off regardless of the state of the set signal. If the reset line is subsequently turned off, then the output will remain off if the set line is unpowered but will turn on if the set line is powered.

Manual Operation[]
A powered latch can also be turned on and off manually whenever the signals to the set and reset line are the same. When they are opposite, the latch is locked in its current state and cannot be changed manually.

Circuit Behaviors[]
Similar to a redstone repeater, a powered latch can both power opaque blocks and can take signal inputs from opaque blocks. 


 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			Powered Toggle Latch 		 	 
Powered Toggle Latch[]
A powered toggle latch has one input and one output. The output is on the side with the redstone torch. The input is on the opposite side. When a pulse is detected on the input, the power state of the output is toggled (off to on or on to off.) The latch reacts to the ascending edge of the pulse. The latch can also be switched on or off manually regardless of the state of the input signal. Similar to a redstone repeater, a powered toggle latch can both power opaque blocks and can take signal inputs from opaque blocks. 

History[]

Pulse Extender and Repeater can now be inverted.
Redstone Link range changed to 256.
0.4:
Added Pulse Extender.
Adjustable Pulse Repeater functionality given to Pulse Repeater.
0.2.4: Redstone link receivers now emit their signal with the level of the strongest transmitter of the same frequency
0.2: Added Analog Lever, Powered Latch, Powered Toggle Latch, and Adjustable Pulse Repeater.

Redstone Contacts facing Redstone Contacts on an assembled Elevator will become Elevator Contacts. Redstone Contacts placed in the same X and Z coordinates and the same direction as an Elevator Contact will also become Elevator Contacts. Successfully implemented elevator contacts can be identified by the rose-coloured back as shown in the screenshot. This side should face away from the contact side.
