 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Value Settings Screen of a Valve Handle. 		 	 
The Value Settings Screen is used to adjust the settings of various blocks. 

Usage[]
The Value Settings screen can be accessed by looking at an area on various placed blocks. It appears on the block as a square 4x4 pixels in size, much like a Filter. While looking at it, the block's current settings may be displayed. 
Hold right-click to access the screen, move the mouse or scroll to change the settings, and release the interact key to confirm the new settings.  If the Value Settings adjusts a number, the sneak key can be held to snap to multiples of 8. For blocks that adjust rotation speed, there are two lanes for either rotation direction. Certain blocks, such as Linear Chassis, require a Wrench in hand for the Value Settings Screen to be visible.
Most Value Settings can be copied and pasted with a Clipboard.

The Valve Handle functions much like the Hand Crank, though the amount and direction it rotates with one use can be adjusted in its Value Settings Screen. Usage[]
Mirroring Blocks[]
The wand has a range of 50 blocks.
Shift right click to adjust the wand's settings. It can be set to "Mirror Once, Rectangular, or Octagonal," and told what axis to mirror along.
Right click on the ground to place the wand. Right click again to place it elsewhere. While on the Mirror Once or Rectangular settings, the orientation can also be adjusted in-world. Right click on the air or remove the Wand from the hotbar to remove the wand from the world. 
Place or destroy blocks around the wand to have it mirror the action to the other side(s). Placing takes the appropriate blocks from the inventory, and destroying spawns all the items at the block destroyed by the player.

The Water Wheel is a source of rotational power. It generates Rotational Force when water flows over it.  
Due to the fact that the materials required to craft it are easily accessible, the Water Wheel serves as the simplest automatic generator and can be made very early in the game.  
Total stress capacity can be increased by adding more wheels in parallel.

Crafting[]

Large Water Wheel

Usage[]
When water flows over a Water Wheel, it will begin to rotate. This rotational power can be conveyed to other Components from the Water Wheels' Shaft.
Water Wheels can also be powered by Lava, Chocolate, and Bubble Columns.
As long as the water flows around the wheel in mostly one direction, the Wheel will generate Rotational Force.

Appearance[]
The Water Wheel's appearance can be changed by right-clicking any type of Planks on it. The items will not be consumed. Each texture is automatically generated using the planks and logs of a wood type, allowing for some compatibility with other mods.

 	 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 	 
Advancements[]

Advancements


Name

Description

Requirements


Harnessing Hydraulics

Place a Water Wheel and try getting it to spin!

Be within 5 blocks when a Water Wheel begins to spin.


Tasteful Power (hidden)

Run a Water Wheel with molten Chocolate.

Be within 5 blocks when Chocolate starts up a Water Wheel.


Magma Wheel (hidden)

This shouldn't have worked.

Be within 5 blocks when Lava starts up a Water Wheel.

Output[]
The direction of rotation of the water wheel corresponds to the net flow of fluid around the wheel. For the standard water wheel, the 4 blocks adjacent to the wheel are checked for fluid flow while for the large water wheel, the 12 blocks surrounding the center 3x3 frame are checked. The strength of the flow of each block does not influence the result, only the direction.
The standard water wheel outputs rotation at 8 RPM and 256 SU. The large water wheel outputs rotation at 4 RPM and 512 SU.

Pre 0.5.1[]





The following section describes content that exists only in outdated versions of CreateThis feature used to be in the mod but has since been removed.

The water wheel has a correct direction of rotation, shown by how the blades are oriented. Water flowing the wrong way around the wheel causes it to produce less rotational speed and stress capacity than if the water was flowing the right way. Having water flowing in the opposite directions might slow down the rotational speed or even stop it. The direction of rotation is counter-clockwise when placed standing, or clockwise when crouching.

Obtaining[]
Crafting[]


Name
Ingredients
Recipe




Weighted  Ejector

Golden Sheet +Depot +Cogwheel





Usage[]
To select a target, sneak+use the ejector on the desired target block, then place the ejector some distance away. The target must be in a straight axial (on the same X/Z axis) line from where the Ejector is placed. The maximum range of the selection target is 32 blocks horizontally, and infinite blocks vertically, but placing the target higher than 33-35 blocks will only result in a slight increase in launch height.
The ejector can be recharged by connecting rotational power to its input. Recharge time increases with distance, but can be sped up by increasing the input's RPM. Rotating the input the wrong way will also increase the recharge time slightly--with the ejector facing to the right, the correct input direction is counter-clockwise.
The amount of items ejected can be adjusted in the Value Settings Screen accessible from the front, back, or the gold square under the ejector's plate. The Ejector will wait until it has the appropriate amount of items before launching them.

Tips:[]
Items flung still collide with blocks, but cannot be picked up or stopped by the player.
If the Ejector is rotated or moved via contraption or wrench, the target moves with it.
If the player is wearing Elytra, the ejector will deploy the elytra automatically, allowing them to fly great distances.

A windmill generates Rotational Force. It is composed of a Windmill Bearing (or Mechanical Bearing in pre 0.3 versions) and at least 8 sails or sail-like blocks. Du...
content:
https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Windmill_Bearing_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scene for the Windmill Bearing. 		 	 
A windmill generates Rotational Force. It is composed of a Windmill Bearing (or Mechanical Bearing in pre 0.3 versions) and at least 8 sails or sail-like blocks. Due to the easy access to its components, the windmill along with the Water Wheel are the earliest automatic power generators in the game.
Sail-like blocks include:

Windmill Sails
Windmill Sail Frames
Wool Blocks
Copycat Panels equipped with another sail-like block
Contents

1 Usage
2 Advancements
3 Gallery
4 History



Usage[]
A windmill is created by attaching any block to the front of the Windmill Bearing to act as a hub, then attaching multiple sail blocks to the hub bock.  The Windmill Bearing comes with glue already on the face to which the hub block attaches. When attaching sails and sail frames, they attach even without glue. Wool and additional blocks may be attached with Super Glue. The additional blocks are decorative only. Only the sail-like blocks generate power.  
Sail blocks include Windmill Sails, Sail Frames, and Wool blocks. The windmill's angular velocity increases by 1 RPM each time the number of sail-like blocks increases by 8, only starting to rotate once there are 8 sail-like blocks. The amount of stress generated is 512 su per RPM. Sails will automatically connect to each other and to blocks that have already been attached. The sails can be placed in any configuration; the shape does not matter.   
Right-click the Windmill Bearing anywhere but the center with an empty hand to start the windmill.  To stop it, right-click on the block with an empty hand again. To change the spin direction, right-click and hold on the center of the bearing where a circular arrow appears. Hold down the right mouse key and either scroll the wheel or move the mouse left and right to select the direction.

 	https://create.fandom.com/wiki/File:Windmill_Bearing_Ponder.mp4 	 	 		 			 		 		 		 			The Ponder scene for the Windmill Bearing. 		 	 
In order to begin generating power, a Windmill Bearing must have at least eight Sails, Sail Frames, Wool blocks, or Copycat Panels equipped with wool attached. Any other block can also be attached with Super Glue, though it will not yield any benefit. This will create a Windmill.
By default, the Windmill Bearing spins clockwise, though this can be changed to counter-clockwise with the Wrench. For every 8 sail-type blocks connected to the Windmill Bearing, it gains 1 RPM and 512su (8-15 sails gives 512su at 1 RPM, 16-23 gives 1024su at 2 RPM, etc.). A Windmill will produce a maximum of 8192su (128 sail-type blocks).

Usage[]
Using a Wrench on a component will rotate the component around the face with which you interacted.
Using a Wrench on a component, redstone component, rail or vanilla rail variant will dismantle it and place it in your inventory. Any block which can be rotated or otherwise interacted with using right click must be dismantled while sneaking.
Hovering over certain configurable components will allow configuration by scrolling.
For certain components such as the Linear Chassis, ctrl can be held to configure all connected components at once.

content:
Zinc is a material found in the overworld. It spawns naturally as zinc ore and can be smelted into ingots or crushed into Crushed Zinc Ore.

Items[]
 Zinc Ingot — an item created by smelting zinc ore or crushed zinc ore.
 Crushed Zinc Ore — an item obtained by crushing zinc ore or zinc blocks. Can be smelted into zinc ingots or washed into zinc nuggets.
 Zinc Nugget — an item that can be crafted into a zinc ingot. Can be used to craft the Andesite Alloy.
Blocks[]
 Zinc Ore — an ore found underground, and an item obtained by mining it. Can be smelted into zinc ingots or crushed into crushed zinc ore.
 Block of Zinc — a block used for compact zinc storage, and to create the base/pyramid for a beacon.

Zinc nuggets are small pieces of Zinc that can be obtained through crafting a single zinc ingot. One zinc nugget is equal to a ninth of a zinc ingot. They are used to craft zinc ingots and Andesite Alloy.
Zinc nuggets can serve as a nice alternative method for crafting Andesite Alloy instead of using iron nuggets, as iron has far more uses than zinc.

Obtaining[]
Breaking[]
Zinc ore must be mined with an iron pickaxe or higher, or else it drops nothing. Zinc ore drops 1 Raw Zinc unless the player uses Silk Touch or Fortune.

Hardness3ToolBreaking time[Note 1] Default15 Wooden7.5 Stone3.75 Iron0.75 Diamond0.6 Netherite0.5 Golden1.25
↑ Times are for unenchanted tools as wielded by players with no status effects, measured in seconds. For more information, see Breaking § Speed.


Natural Generation[]
Zinc Ore can generate in the Overworld in the form of Blobs. ( Ore_(feature) )
It can be found between Y levels -63 to 70.
